What we can still learn from Washington and Hamilton's military service. | | | Jun 23 | | | | | | | | | | | | When I returned from Iraq in 2004, I lived in New Hope, Pennsylvania, just a few miles from the stretch of the Delaware River where George Washington famously crossed on Christmas night in 1776. Every morning, I drove past the spot where Washington loaded 2,400 freezing soldiers into small boats and led them across an ice-choked river toward a surprise attack on Hessian forces in Trenton. For a long time, I thought of it as a historical landmark. But driving past it regularly made me think about what had actually happened there. The crossing was a desperate gamble by a commander who understood that doing nothing was the surest path to defeat. By Christmas 1776, the Revolution was hanging by a thread. The crossing didn't just help save the Revolution. It helps explain the country that emerged from it. As America approaches its 250th anniversary, we owe it to our country to recognize how profoundly military service shaped the men who created this nation. While we often think of America's founding purely as the product of intellectual statesmen, many of the ideas that gave birth to the United States were forged directly from the battlefield. No two figures illustrate that better than George Washington and Alexander Hamilton. They were more than political theorists who happened to serve in uniform. They were soldiers who helped build a political system based on what they had watched succeed and fail during war. Washington and Hamilton were hardly the only soldiers who helped build America's political system. After the Revolution, went on to serve in the House of Representatives, and five of the first six Speakers of the House had served in the war. This generation of veterans had watched soldiers go hungry because a new government lacked the capacity to do its most basic jobs. And they had watched a revolution nearly collapse because leaders couldn't coordinate on resources, funding, or strategy. That's why the country they built for us emphasized strong institutions and robust personal freedoms. The American founding was shaped by men who had seen firsthand what happens when government fails. Two hundred and fifty years later, that's still a lesson worth remembering. The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. George Washington and Alexander Hamilton could not have come from more different worlds. Washington was born into wealth and privilege on a scale that would be comparable to Jeff Bezos level net worth today. He essentially ran a plantation empire at Mount Vernon. Hamilton, meanwhile, was an orphan from the Caribbean who came to New York as a teenager with no money but big dreams and confidence. Their two stories are near opposites. One was born at the top and had everything to lose. The other was born at the bottom and had almost nothing tangible. Yet despite their vastly different origins, both found themselves transformed by the same experience of war. The military has always been one of the few institutions capable of bringing people from radically different backgrounds into the same reality. For Hamilton, the Continental Army was one of the few places in eighteenth-century America where talent could matter more than pedigree. Washington's decision to lead the Revolution was extraordinary given his wealth and his age. When the Revolution began in 1775, Washington was 43, which was no spring chicken back then. He had already achieved the success and status most people spend a lifetime pursuing. He could've easily lived a life of comfort. Instead, he spent the next eight years fighting for a cause that, for much of the war, appeared destined to fail. Men of Washington's wealth rarely interacted with ordinary laborers as equals, much less shared hardship with them. The Revolution changed that. For eight years, Washington lived among soldiers whose lives bore little resemblance to his own--farmers, laborers, tradesmen, immigrants, and young men with little wealth and even less certainty about the future. He watched them endure hunger, disease, brutal cold, and death in pursuit of an idea. That experience fundamentally changed his understanding of leadership. Before the war, Washington was a wealthy Virginia planter whose world was largely defined by land and status. After the war, he emerged as a national leader with a broader understanding of the people he served and the sacrifices they had made to create a country. In some ways, that lesson had been 20 years in the making. It's easy to forget that Washington didn't begin his military career fighting against the British. He began it fighting for them two decades earlier. As a young officer during the French and Indian War, Washington admired the British Army, then the most powerful military force in the world, and hoped to earn a commission in its regular ranks. He never did. Instead, he learned a frustrating lesson about status and power in the British Empire: colonial officers were rarely treated as the equals of their British-born counterparts, regardless of talent or accomplishment. The irony is hard to miss. Twenty years after being rejected from the British Army, Washington led the ragged, underfunded force that defeated it. Hamilton underwent a different transformation. The military gave him something he had never had before: belonging and opportunity. In 18th century America, land and family name determined almost everything. The Continental Army was one of the few institutions that partially suspended those distinctions. A Caribbean orphan and the son of a wealthy Virginia planter could find themselves standing in the same ranks, enduring the same hardships, and fighting for the same cause. That shared sacrifice created a sense of common purpose that civilian life rarely produced. In many ways, it still does. Military service remains one of the few experiences that brings Americans from vastly different backgrounds into the same mission and asks them to depend on one another. Hamilton proved that talent could overcome upbringing. The Continental Army didn't care about his abysmal start. It cared whether he could do the job. At just 21, Hamilton commanded artillery during some of the Revolution's most important campaigns, including Trenton and Princeton. He proved so fearless under fire that Washington pulled him onto his personal staff. Before the war, Hamilton was a brilliant nobody. By the end of it, he had become one of the most trusted members of Washington's inner circle. As Washington's aide-de-camp, Hamilton drafted orders, coordinated communications, managed crises, and helped hold together the administrative machinery of the Continental Army. The position gave him access to the most influential minds in America. But access wasn't the only thing Hamilton gained. He also received a firsthand education in institutional failure. From Washington's side, he watched Congress struggle to raise money, supply troops, and coordinate the war effort. He saw soldiers go unpaid, provisions arrive late, and military strategy undermined by political dysfunction. Those experiences shaped everything he built afterward. The future Treasury Secretary spent much of his career creating the financial infrastructure the young republic lacked during the Revolution: a national bank, a stable currency, and a functioning credit system. Hamilton wasn't solving an abstract economic problem. He was trying to ensure the United States would never again be too weak to sustain itself. By the time the war ended, Hamilton knew everyone who mattered--and everyone who mattered knew him. That remains one of military service's most important contributions to American life. It is still one of the few institutions where a person can arrive with little more than talent, discipline, and ambition and earn a seat at the table. * The lessons both men learned during the war would shape the country they built afterward. Today it's easy to forget how fragile the United States looked after the Revolution. The Articles of Confederation gave almost no power to the central government. The arrangement sounded appealing in theory. Washington and Hamilton knew better. Their support for a stronger federal government was shaped by their experience at war. They had seen what happened when leaders lacked the authority, resources, and coordination necessary to govern effectively. They had lived the alternative. And perhaps nothing proves that more than what Washington did with power once he had it. History is full of military leaders who won wars and decided the country belonged to them. Julius Caesar didn't surrender power. Napoleon didn't either. Neither did Oliver Cromwell. Washington did, though. Twice. After the Revolution, some wanted him to become something close to a king. After two terms as president, he could have remained in office indefinitely. Instead, he walked away, establishing a precedent that would become one of the defining features of the American experiment. That decision may have been the single most important act of leadership in American history. I doubt he makes it without eight years alongside men who had nothing but gave everything for an idea. He learned that the country didn't belong to its wealthiest citizens. It belonged to all of them. Neither man was perfect, nor was the country they built. A nation dedicated to liberty coexisted with slavery, and Washington himself participated in that system. That contradiction would eventually tear the country apart. Recognizing the founders' achievements does not require ignoring their failures. The freedoms we enjoy today were secured by ordinary people willing to sacrifice for an extraordinary cause. Our independence was won not by famous names alone, but by 250,000 soldiers whose courage and sacrifice made the country possible. Let's remember them and their sacrifices on our 250th birthday, and never take it for granted that we're all here to help form a more perfect Union. Hey folks,
When we were kids, we learned about the Scientific Method. My teacher had a big poster with all of the steps:
💡 Find a question to investigate.
📝 Make predictions.
🔬 Gather data.
📊 Analyze the data.
🤔 Draw conclusions.
It’s the exact approach I applied in medical school and in diagnosing and caring for patients in the intensive care unit. It’s the same way I lead, now, in Congress.
When I was a kid, my grandmother lived with us, and she had diabetes. I learned to dress her wounds and wondered, why don’t we all have the same access to medical help?
At first, I assumed there had to be a simple explanation. But as I moved through medical school and treated patients, I gathered the evidence.
I saw insurance companies deny care. I saw drug companies jack up prices. I saw families take on debt, work extra jobs, and postpone treatment just to stay afloat. Now, the MAGA movement is cutting programs like Medicaid and SNAP, and it’s just getting worse.
The data is clear.
And the conclusion is simple: healthcare is a human right, and every single American deserves affordable, high-quality healthcare.

Instead, they're whining.

| | Dear Friend,

How much do you know about the Electoral College?

It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future.

You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president.

**Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. **

**That 's why I hope you'll take our National Quiz on Presidential Selection today.** It's a quick and engaging way to test your own understanding of how our presidents are elected.

**You can take your quiz by using the secure link below:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/sPIHZEW6v8vFre_y3FTVeOCUtgpJOOrMyMFAY2nWu1Kx3sjbs9DNUZs7BfG2fo-iJy-tvjnlT81ezHvlQVEH_oj8uIpyzLuTUiGf7gyPFv__d9ddX3SggDFO1m9rO2_incyUiUsmOFK-pSV1voYAOU2ated2drNL1oor7bgxWnjCFMxuY-NzwAb5Nb1W8LxCFVkaZcQsoxdKfJtFehWpanIOmbRV2jBrbMTyYetVDXMFwY0DAeHCjo0rGCrhfDmscj-eWpzd4Xt-J1-xj820lE4i8uNP60YEQChOJMxrnOwCL55N2c2TCPFnzjog3qwpWhk6HJFH1STjEITf0rx6SWgrnjyl7ZYgwxScUZdN-488-BjPA-KyIVt6CtcMdtYjLUFe4sBp9ZWteyTubZY_73UoQTR3waQYZ8OvKtYCdfOtIsFyUe6Lvu7Hpwxf64FDz78CB3imhTZjscAzA1OCgDrnRwZcEixo2jl94KKkWxNVFNPkHCMfzIjitKmnvIo0wTB3ZRhyG9t-ujg3jY9Czg2KC7xa6cyKCXYPZleO_X1tSPGDCnI5IjTcYs3zL0k4YX3bcPm3lHntdv_EGMPxhlhXGmRJxWIUoLmwXDEibRL6JbrUAK5cpZ7LmEciCVZ_RNHqnFqUqPpHWJfjNAbrW2SRqrBDeSW-Duiec8zMuG36ZFyRIcz2VFGkOs5ahws3D-TwB8dRN4ykgyK9qFN6YKoVizLjG_MavIRlGwq8gZ2MLrACTi5v5tkTGemIK1isq_gq4uGCPJhlTCvv1uhWtlLWXESN5q9wUxaNW_6zBHLZn2JiS8SInbjwNpMBc1hZ2w/IRLAFUAtIPi2LANpVwrN2WVm4-_a8-Ze/22)

For most of our history, the Electoral College was uncontroversial. It was understood to be a safeguard for free and representative government.

**But today, dozens of states have joined together to undermine this key constitutional protection.**

The push to "move beyond" the Constitution stems from the failure of too many schools to teach American civics properly. Many citizens today don't fully understand the importance of the Constitution and the Electoral College in preserving liberty.

To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, **reaching and teaching millions** of Americans in all 50 states.

When you take the **National Quiz on Presidential Selection** , you'll gain a clearer understanding of how the Electoral College upholds liberty--and you'll have the opportunity to **share this** information with your fellow Americans.

So please take your **National Quiz on Presidential Selection**. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

**You can take the quiz using the secure link I 've provided below: **

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/bTfrYdg8Gm5e7SVLAS7og0wqDwB13WmTaytEDMmCGK57PVBaU9unujZaO4sbR7JArA5iBRqeQHWSXLv71R6vOruNzWwkjCyA2W1xNwLbKytVM-VsWSoiCHlr_DYzh0pAijs30I82CJrTjELOHiUjiMGYoknxWD66MaDrPi66nFnnEs5vY_1vHwjAd9cz3yGFtbvfDXkn5uoUgtPIBg0GXa8yv5QRNjWjbZbpm5M3bJyEUwhpyuiwUb2d8mcpa7Dt3PquWTsX-e5-u4aRLQGOY5Qcxo9NUzA-EokilPqv9RJQJTRKSelL1c1pMWX074qqzxQFD5vBAnLp0QSK2zkDY6-_WHB6Gk5b8GOhcuWHMdL3g2PfdP3Ifitizj-Aa9YmAQUwoB_BZk95Ddi1bpymVdET-yeF3iHpaVxQHhkJx03Fz1Oqp-3tHDcWD7O-OB1-e1rjk9PZH0DzIeXSs-ZVvwdQCDk7mjIg3Y5V3EeAWWDw3D98PoeJB8C0wKsre9It5wccvCe7LsKdpPQIm9CCb2uNJBE6y0VGc35HqYkUANmV7T20CD4kOrdN59S14Mv02hzZYlizVWizxYyw5WSP7-MDqzoynVuLmfPeZe5Mj2TmNhpGK4YXTcjVFBtayxpecS-8ajfQ_5jLpJiXpl7uwyGznzpxxkt8hpjRJy0xQhcsCxkl8LC08RfH-NjHDNvXMjEA6CBYYlLLj5jRVYvPYU1la2v3TKQ7iboZzZNvc1Nbdye_qcblrBZB2j7uVoT3HlM65mbVLlyyyPdUu4FRXSMW_aMFAMihTmFoVRj1egAzvNqWTmwAplpnRR29fKkvKQ/2Thi-kk3U1j6SHL7-zPMijW-N6ZF4M4i/22)

**As a thank-you for taking the quiz, I 'll send you a free 12-minute video with a Hillsdale College professor that explains the history and purpose of the Electoral College. **

The video provides a concise, engaging, and insightful overview of the Electoral College and its significance. It would be a great resource to send to a friend or a family member!

One other thing.

Hillsdale refuses EVERY PENNY of government funding--even indirectly through student loans or grants--so that we can pursue truth and defend liberty independent of meddling bureaucrats in Washington, D.C. That's why your support matters so much.

So, after you take your quiz, please also consider giving a **tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, or even $100** to help us share this video with millions of Americans--especially young people who don't understand how the Constitution preserves liberty through the Electoral College. Your gift also funds our other nationwide educational outreach.

Thank you for standing with Hillsdale College in the effort to educate Americans about the Constitution and safeguard the principles of liberty. Good luck on the quiz and enjoy your video!

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement

If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | | | Dear Friend, How much do you know about the Electoral College? It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future. You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president. Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. That 's why I hope you'll take our National Quiz on Presidential Selection today. It's a quick and engaging way to test your own understanding of how our presidents are elected. You can take your quiz by using the secure link below: For most of our history, the Electoral College was uncontroversial. It was understood to be a safeguard for free and representative government. But today, dozens of states have joined together to undermine this key constitutional protection. The push to "move beyond" the Constitution stems from the failure of too many schools to teach American civics properly. Many citizens today don't fully understand the importance of the Constitution and the Electoral College in preserving liberty. To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, reaching and teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states. When you take the National Quiz on Presidential Selection , you'll gain a clearer understanding of how the Electoral College upholds liberty--and you'll have the opportunity to share this information with your fellow Americans. So please take your National Quiz on Presidential Selection. It will only take a few minutes of your time. You can take the quiz using the secure link I 've provided below: As a thank-you for taking the quiz, I 'll send you a free 12-minute video with a Hillsdale College professor that explains the history and purpose of the Electoral College. Hillsdale refuses EVERY PENNY of government funding--even indirectly through student loans or grants--so that we can pursue truth and defend liberty independent of meddling bureaucrats in Washington, D.C. That's why your support matters so much. So, after you take your quiz, please also consider giving a tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, or even $100 to help us share this video with millions of Americans--especially young people who don't understand how the Constitution preserves liberty through the Electoral College. Your gift also funds our other nationwide educational outreach. Thank you for standing with Hillsdale College in the effort to educate Americans about the Constitution and safeguard the principles of liberty. Good luck on the quiz and enjoy your video! **** A memo from the Justice Department recently argued that states do not have to provide in-home or community-based care to people with disabilities. The disabled community deserves to work and live with their family and friends without the fear of being forced into an institution that does not have the resources to make their lives fulfilled. **Without the federal government requiring that states help disabled people integrate into their communities, this has the momentum to create a second-class citizenship for disabled Americans.****** We could see states plunging disabled folks into darkness, to keep them out of sight. clean_body: | | | This should worry every single American. A memo from the Justice Department recently argued that states do not have to provide in-home or community-based care to people with disabilities. The disabled community deserves to work and live with their family and friends without the fear of being forced into an institution that does not have the resources to make their lives fulfilled. Without the federal government requiring that states help disabled people integrate into their communities, this has the momentum to create a second-class citizenship for disabled Americans.**** We could see states plunging disabled folks into darkness, to keep them out of sight. Advocates are continuing to bring this and many other issues to the Trump administration, but unfortunately, the disabled community just doesn’t have major political power like the tobacco or gun lobby. body:
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3432%2E21716%2ER4yZOx)
Friend,
Progress in public service doesn't happen by default. It happens when leaders consistently show up prepared, do the hard work, and bring people together around a common purpose.
**Sarah McBride does that every single day, which is why I'm proud to endorse her re-election campaign.**
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260623-1.Cp5z-g&refcode=em20260623-3432&t=2&akid=3432%2E21716%2ER4yZOx)
Delaware voters made history when they sent Sarah to Washington. But what matters even more than the historic nature of her service is her effectiveness in Congress – fighting for her constituents, pushing to lower costs, and showing that good leadership can emerge in difficult times.
Sarah is exactly the kind of public servant we need more of: principled, effective, and relentlessly focused on results over headlines. She's not in this for the politics of it all. She's in it to get results for the people she serves.
This November, we have a real opportunity to flip the House and elect a Democratic majority that can hold this administration accountable. But it won’t happen on its own. We need to do the work of protecting and re-electing great leaders like Sarah.
[**Friend, I hope you'll join me. If you're able, please consider making a contribution of $5 – or whatever you can – to support Sarah's campaign today.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260623-1.Cp5z-g&refcode=em20260623-3432&amount=5&t=3&akid=3432%2E21716%2ER4yZOx)

Pete Buttigieg

name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
subject: One week to hit our goals
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
One week from today, Equal Opportunity Now will face our first end-of-quarter fundraising deadline.
It may look like just another date on the calendar. But for a brand-new group like ours, it means much more than that.
The number we report after June 30th will be the first real measure of whether we have the grassroots strength to take on powerful interests, support bold leaders, and fight for an economy where every American gets a fair shot.
I started Equal Opportunity Now because I have seen what opportunity can mean for a family.
My family came to this country with very little. For a time, we relied on public housing and food stamps. My parents worked hard and believed America would meet them halfway.
And because people before us fought to build a country where families like mine could get ahead, it did.
But that promise is slipping away for too many Americans.
Working people are being asked to pay more for groceries, housing, healthcare, and childcare while the federal minimum wage remains frozen at $7.25 an hour.
Billionaires and corporations keep finding new ways to rig the rules in their favor.
Donald Trump and his MAGA allies are tearing apart the programs families rely on and targeting anyone who does not fit their narrow vision of who belongs in this country.
Equal Opportunity Now was created to fight back.
We are building the resources to support leaders and causes that will raise wages, create good-paying jobs, defend workers, hold corrupt politicians and corporate bad actors accountable, and make sure opportunity is not reserved for people born into wealth or power.
But we have to prove that real people are ready to stand behind that mission.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now reach our first end-of-quarter goal before June 30th? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE BEFORE THE DEADLINE >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
We have seven days to show the political world what we are capable of.
Let’s make them count.
-- Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

Equal Opportunity Now is d/b/a Reviving American Jobs Again PAC (RAJA PAC)

name: The Turning Point USA Team
subject: Why JD Vance’s story meant so much to Charlie Kirk
body:
Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance

| | | |
---
| | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

subject: “This is NOT supposed to be a close race!”

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
And MAGA is absolutely shocked.
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment.
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars — the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment — if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable — everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.
Will you chip in $50, $25, or $10 to help us seize this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
CHIP IN TO FLIP THIS SENATE SEAT! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
We have the opportunity to pull off something historic in Louisiana that will do a whole lot of good for people here. I couldn’t be more grateful to have you fighting alongside me.
Jamie Davis
Democrat for U.S. Senate

Children with disabilities deserve to be seen for their potential, their talents, and their futures. They deserve the same opportunity to learn, grow, and thrive as every other child.

_But Donald Trump’s decision to empower RFK with managing these programs is a fundamental shift away from that principle._

Instead of viewing children with disabilities as students first, RFK views them as medical conditions to be managed. **But they’re so much more than that — and I’m going to fight for them each and every day in Congress.**

As an educator and a mom, I know firsthand how transformative it can be when our children receive the support, resources, and opportunities they deserve.

_And as a scientist, I'm deeply concerned by RFK Jr.'s long history of spreading misinformation about autism and other developmental disabilities._

**I'm running for Congress because I believe every child deserves access to a great education — and now more than ever before, we need leaders who see the dignity and potential in every student.** [**But I need your help to get there. name: Courier Newsroom
subject: Trump’s peeling paint job is everything
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1003&refcode=20260623_Pool&akid=65%2E344797%2EQZwVCU ]COURIER Newsroom

Peter,

Trump is a terrible executive. From his own failed businesses to the war
in Iran, he has spent a lifetime finding new, spectacular ways to show
just how unfit he is to run anything, let alone a country.

So when news broke that the $14M paint job Trump ordered for the Lincoln
Memorial Reflecting Pool was already peeling, you probably weren't
surprised.

So why does this keep happening?

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20260623_Pool&akid=65%2E344797%2EQZwVCU ]We'll tell you why in a moment, but if you believe in
funding a newsroom that is designed to reach Americans in the spaces they
actually read the news, please chip in $25 today.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1006&refcode=20260623_Pool&akid=65%2E344797%2EQZwVCU ]→ Chip in $25

When news first broke that Donald Trump would paint the pool "American
flag blue," he said it would cost $1.8 million.

Then the cost hit $14 million, on a no-bid contract handed to a company
Trump said had done pool work at his own golf club.

Within a week the water turned green and the paint started peeling off in
sheets.

Rush the job, skip the process, cash in with friends, declare victory,
watch it fall apart. It's Trump's presidency in a nutshell.

Now Trump blames "vandals," with no evidence, and is draining the whole
thing to start over.

The press actually covered all of it admirably. They questioned the cost,
skewered the sweetheart contract, and pointed out how the project would do
nothing to repair the pool for the long term.

But it barely registered. Why? Because a quarter of the country no longer
trusts a word the media says, and the majority don't even get their news
from traditional sources.

That's the real fight. Not that Trump does this. That the reporting
doesn't reach Americans because they stopped listening.

COURIER exists to change that. We go where people actually are, in the
feeds and inboxes, and earn back the trust legacy media lost.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1007&refcode=20260623_Pool&akid=65%2E344797%2EQZwVCU ]We're funding a new kind of progressive newsroom, one that isn't afraid
to tell the truth about this president. But we're behind on our $75,000
end-of-quarter goal, and the deadline is closing in.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1008&refcode=20260623_Pool&akid=65%2E344797%2EQZwVCU ]→ Chip in $25

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1009&refcode=20260623_Pool&akid=65%2E344797%2EQZwVCU ]→ Or give whatever you can

In solidarity,
The COURIER Team

communicate with grassroots supporters like you.

_Hi y’all, it’s Andy Beshear and I wanted to share a message from my friend Keisha Lance Bottoms. Keisha could be Georgia’s first Black woman governor and our chance to finally flip this seat. Please consider contributing to her campaign.

body:
Hi Peter,

I have an important message for you: Thank you.

This campaign isn’t just about me — it’s about showing the strength of the incredible movement we’ve created for a better, stronger Pennsylvania.

Thank you for trusting me to fight for you in D.C., for standing by me through every tough race, and for showing up when it matters most.

From serving on the Scranton School Board to working in the PA Auditor General’s office to serving as Mayor of Scranton (Paige Against the Machine forever!) — my mission has always been to take on corruption and put our families, neighbors, and communities first.

My public service has been dedicated to rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in government.

Now, I’m ready to take that fight to a place that needs it badly: a Congress controlled by special interests and self-serving politicians who put the people last.

Whether you’ve supported us financially or are supporting our campaign in other ways, you’ve proven that people power beats big money and Washington special interests every time. If you can, consider chipping in now to bring us one step closer to winning this race.

name: Elizabeth For Viginia
subject: Celebrating Women In The Military
body:
Hegseth Can Attack Women In The Military, But I Will Always Honor Them

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/elizabethforvirginia/celebrating-women-in-the-military?e=2f83c585b2)
---
|
---
[|

| | | | | |
# _Honoring Progress And Defending Opportunity_
---
| |
**This week, I am traveling to Washington, D.C. to participate in a Congressional Roundtable on women’s leadership in the military as we celebrate a remarkable milestone: the 50th anniversary of the first class of women graduating from West Point.**
**It is an opportunity to reflect on how far we have come. Fifty years ago, those trailblazing women helped redefine what leadership in America could look like. Through determination and courage, they proved that talent and commitment, not gender, are what matter most when serving our nation.**
**Their legacy is worth celebrating. And for me, it’s personal. As a former Tank Commander in the U.S Army, their leadership is beyond inspiring. But anniversaries like this are also a reminder that progress is never guaranteed.**
**Recent actions by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to roll back initiatives that have helped broaden leadership opportunities and reevaluate promotion pathways raise serious concerns about the future of military leadership. At a time when our nation faces growing challenges around the world, we should be focused on attracting and retaining the very best people to serve.**
**America’s military is strongest when every qualified service member has the opportunity to succeed based on merit and performance. When talented individuals question whether opportunities are being limited or whether their contributions are fully valued, it can affect our national security in real time.**
**This isn't just about fairness. It's about readiness. The strength of our armed forces comes from the quality of the people who wear the uniform. Our nation cannot afford to lose talented leaders or discourage future generations from answering the call to serve.**
**The story of those first women graduates at West Point reminds us of something important: when America expands opportunity, we become stronger. When we invest in talent and leadership wherever we find it, we all benefit.**
**That is a lesson worth honoring, and a future worth fighting for.**
**Thank you for being part of this effort.****Elizabeth**

name: Autism Health
subject: Webinar is This Saturday! Don't Miss the Premiere of SHINE!
body:
June Monthly Webinar with Dr. Kurt Woeller

Join us this Saturday, June 27th at 9:00 AM PST / 12:00 PM EST for an informative webinar featuring Dr. Kurt Woeller titled:

Methylcobalamin (Methyl-B12) Therapy: Remembering an Innovative Autism Intervention

Methylcobalamin (Methyl-B12) therapy has been one of the most widely discussed biomedical interventions in autism care over the past two decades. In this presentation, Dr. Woeller will review the history of Methyl-B12 therapy, the science behind its use, its role in supporting methylation and neurological function, and why it continues to be an important topic for families and practitioners working with individuals on the autism spectrum.

Kurt N. Woeller, DO, FMAPS, is a Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, integrative and functional medicine physician, and biomedical autism treatment specialist who has been in clinical practice for over three decades. He currently serves as the Chief Medical Officer for Mosaic Diagnostics and is recognized internationally for his work educating families and healthcare professionals on autism, neurodevelopmental disorders, and integrative medical approaches.

Whether you are a parent, caregiver, practitioner, or advocate, this webinar offers a valuable opportunity to learn from one of the field's most experienced clinicians.

Register using the link below to reserve your spot.
REGISTER HERE (https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_FdkMwMeUQSyr3GFzDQLx1Q?mc_cid=d60178f003&mc_eid=UNIQID#/registration)

** Don't Miss the Premiere of SHINE!
------------------------------------------------------------

If you've followed the work of filmmaker Mikki Willis, you won't want to miss this special event.

At just 14 years old, Azai Willis has created his second film, SHINE, an award-winning documentary short that asks a powerful question: What if your thoughts and choices were never fully your own? In just six minutes, SHINE explores what may be contributing to the growing depression, anxiety, and disconnection that so many young people are experiencing today and challenges us to rethink what has become accepted as normal.

The film recently won Best Documentary Short at the Santa Monica International Film Festival and is now being made available to the public for the very first time.

On June 30th, Mikki Willis will host a free live premiere of SHINE, followed by a candid father and son conversation exploring the inspiration behind the film, the challenges facing today's youth, and the importance of critical thinking, connection, and purpose. The event will also include a live Q&A session with the audience.

This will be the first opportunity for anyone outside the festival circuit to view the film. Reserve your free seat today and be part of this important conversation.

Register using the link below.
REGISTER HERE (https://mikkiwillis.com/shine?mc_cid=d60178f003&mc_eid=UNIQID)

Save the Date: Cocktails for A Cause
https://ahsconference.com/?mc_cid=d60178f003&mc_eid=UNIQID

We are excited to invite you to our upcoming Cocktails for A Cause fundraiser benefiting Autism Health Inc. on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM at The Park Club in Costa Mesa, CA.

Sponsored by Cellular Performance Institute, this special evening will bring together supporters, families, professionals, and community leaders for a night of connection, purpose, and giving back. Guests will enjoy cocktails, networking, inspiring presentations from featured speakers (to be announced), and both a live auction and silent auction filled with exciting items and experiences.

Tickets are $85 per person, and proceeds from the evening will help support Autism Health Inc.’s ongoing mission to provide education, resources, support programs, and outreach for families impacted by autism and neurological conditions.

We hope you will join us for this meaningful evening as we come together to make a difference in the lives of so many families.
BUY TICKETS HERE (https://givebutter.com/cocktails-4-a-cause?gbtid=6973b353-2ebb-4a2b-be6f-b0a7a0f1fab1&mc_cid=d60178f003&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** Summer Movie Fundraiser to Support Autism Health
------------------------------------------------------------

Looking for a fun way to support Autism Health this summer? We are excited to partner with GroupRaise and Regal Cinemas for a special fundraising campaign that allows you to enjoy a night at the movies while supporting a great cause.

For just $30 per order, you'll receive a Regal Movie Ticket Bundle that includes two Standard 2D Movie Tickets, redeemable at any Regal theater location nationwide. Best of all, 20% of every purchase will be donated to Autism Health Inc. to help support our educational programs, support groups, webinars, scholarships, and research initiatives.

Did you know that many Regal Cinemas locations also offer Sensory Friendly Screenings? These special screenings are designed to create a more comfortable movie-going experience for individuals with autism and sensory sensitivities, making this fundraiser even more meaningful for our community.

Whether you're planning a family outing, date night, or looking for a unique gift, your purchase helps advance our mission of serving individuals and families impacted by autism and related neurological conditions.

Campaign Ends: Monday, August 17, 2026

Thank you for supporting Autism Health Inc. Every ticket bundle purchased helps us continue making a difference in the lives of families around the world.
BUY TICKETS HERE (https://www.groupraise.com/offer-campaigns/78957-autism-health-inc-regal-fundraising-campaigns?mc_cid=d60178f003&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** AHS Recordings Now Available Online
------------------------------------------------------------

Missed the Autism Health Summit or want to revisit your favorite presentations? We are excited to announce that the full 3-day recordings from the Autism Health Summit are now available for purchase online.

This year’s Summit featured an extraordinary lineup of physicians, researchers, advocates, and thought leaders discussing emerging science, integrative approaches, environmental factors, clinical insights, and practical strategies for individuals impacted by autism and neurological conditions. Now, you can access these powerful presentations from the comfort of your home and learn at your own pace.

We are offering two recording options:
• General Recordings for parents, caregivers, and community members
• Professional Track Recordings for medical professionals seeking to earn 10.5 CME credits

Whether you attended the conference in person or could not join us in San Diego, this is an incredible opportunity to gain access to valuable education and expert insight from the Autism Health Summit.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/pricing-table/?mc_cid=d60178f003&mc_eid=UNIQID)

Please Vote for the 2026 Author of the Year

We are honored to share that Tracy Slepcevic, Co-Founder and President of Autism Health Inc., has been nominated for the 2026 Author of the Year award through the International Impact Book Awards.

Tracy’s bestselling book, Warrior Mom: A Mother's Journey in Healing Her Son with Autism, has inspired and empowered families around the world through her heartfelt story of perseverance, faith, and determination as a mother navigating the autism journey. More than just a memoir, Warrior Mom has become a trusted guidebook for parents seeking hope, practical insight, and encouragement while advocating for their children.

The book has received praise from many respected voices, including the endorsement from Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who described Warrior Mom as:

clean_body: June Monthly Webinar with Dr. Kurt Woeller Join us this Saturday, June 27th at 9:00 AM PST / 12:00 PM EST for an informative webinar featuring Dr. Kurt Woeller titled: Methylcobalamin (Methyl-B12) Therapy: Remembering an Innovative Autism Intervention Methylcobalamin (Methyl-B12) therapy has been one of the most widely discussed biomedical interventions in autism care over the past two decades. In this presentation, Dr. Woeller will review the history of Methyl-B12 therapy, the science behind its use, its role in supporting methylation and neurological function, and why it continues to be an important topic for families and practitioners working with individuals on the autism spectrum. Kurt N. Woeller, DO, FMAPS, is a Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, integrative and functional medicine physician, and biomedical autism treatment specialist who has been in clinical practice for over three decades. He currently serves as the Chief Medical Officer for Mosaic Diagnostics and is recognized internationally for his work educating families and healthcare professionals on autism, neurodevelopmental disorders, and integrative medical approaches. Whether you are a parent, caregiver, practitioner, or advocate, this webinar offers a valuable opportunity to learn from one of the field's most experienced clinicians. Register using the link below to reserve your spot. REGISTER HERE () Don't Miss the Premiere of SHINE! If you've followed the work of filmmaker Mikki Willis, you won't want to miss this special event. At just 14 years old, Azai Willis has created his second film, SHINE, an award-winning documentary short that asks a powerful question: What if your thoughts and choices were never fully your own? In just six minutes, SHINE explores what may be contributing to the growing depression, anxiety, and disconnection that so many young people are experiencing today and challenges us to rethink what has become accepted as normal. The film recently won Best Documentary Short at the Santa Monica International Film Festival and is now being made available to the public for the very first time. On June 30th, Mikki Willis will host a free live premiere of SHINE, followed by a candid father and son conversation exploring the inspiration behind the film, the challenges facing today's youth, and the importance of critical thinking, connection, and purpose. The event will also include a live Q&A session with the audience. This will be the first opportunity for anyone outside the festival circuit to view the film. Reserve your free seat today and be part of this important conversation. Register using the link below. We hope you will join us for this meaningful evening as we come together to make a difference in the lives of so many families. name: Justin Story
subject: Republican Congressional Candidate Justin Story Congratulates Colombia on Historic Election, Celebrates Victory for Freedom and Security
body:
Election after election, our neighbors to the south are rejecting the scourge of socialism that the political left has used to dim the future of those

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18dw07QPzZh?e=90ad5fc3c5&c2id=d60c3f7cebee07fc4dcb3011da999329)
| | | | | |
**PRESS RELEASE**

**Republican Congressional Candidate Justin Story Congratulates Colombia on Historic Election, Celebrates Victory for Freedom and Security** ___“ Election after election, our neighbors to the south are rejecting the scourge of socialism that the political left has used to dim the future of those countries.” _ _– Justin Story****_
---
|
---
| | **June 23, 2026****Contact: justin@votejustinstory.com**
---
| |
(**St. Cloud, Florida**) — Justin Story, retired U.S. Marine Corps F/A-18 fighter pilot and Republican candidate for Florida’s 9th Congressional District, today issued the following statement on this past Sunday’s presidential runoff election in Colombia:
---
| | "Colombians delivered a powerful message this past Sunday: they chose law and order, economic opportunity, and a rejection of failed leftist policies. Right-wing candidate Abelardo de la Espriella secured a victory over his leftist rival.
"Election after election, our neighbors to the south are rejecting the scourge of socialism that the political left has used to dim the future of those countries. Congratulations to the Trump administration for rooting out corrupt and wasteful money that NGOs funnel to those now defunct governments to stay in power. This is another feather in the cap to call for free elections in Venezuela and stop supporting one of the remaining Communist regimes in the area. Stable, free, and capitalist nations south of our border are paramount to the security of our country. Look no further than the Biden administration and the disaster on our southern border.
“My wife, Maria, and her family are firsthand witnesses to the devastating human cost of authoritarian left-wing ideologies. Their story is one of political persecution, property expropriation, and forced exile under the Maduro regime. Colombia’s election is another crack in the dam holding back freedom and opportunity across the hemisphere. Voters rejected the continuation of progressive policies in favor of promises of a tough crackdown on crime, stronger security, and policies to revitalize the economy.
“This victory aligns with a broader regional pushback against socialism and supports pro-freedom, pro-security leadership. De la Espriella’s Trump-backed platform emphasizes practical solutions over ideology, exactly the results-driven approach America needs in Congress.
“To our friends across Central and South America: freedom triumphs when citizens stand firm against tyranny. Central Florida’s vibrant Latin American community knows this truth deeply, and I stand with you in celebrating this win for republican values, security, and prosperity.
“In Congress, I will fight to support strong U.S. partnerships in the region that prioritize national security, combat crime and drugs, and counter authoritarian influences, just as De la Espriella aims to do for Colombia.”
---
| |
Justin Story is a retired U.S. Marine Corps combat veteran and F/A-18 pilot. A proud sixth-generation Central Floridian from St. Cloud, Justin is running for Congress to deliver fiscal responsibility, strong national defense, and results for FL-9 families.
For further information, visit VoteJustinStory.com or contact justin@votejustinstory.com. ###

Soon after President Donald Trump's self-congratulatory tour for "ending" the Gaza war last October, replete with ceremonies in which various kings, emirs, and presidents praised him, Israel made clear it had no intention of respecting the terms of the deal. It continued to kill Palestinians on a near daily basis and began limiting the entry of the agreed upon life essentials to the Strip stipulated in the ceasefire agreement.
Nonetheless, Trump pulled off a coup the following month when he got the UN Security Council to endorse his Gaza plan. In an unprecedented move, the council endorsed the deployment of an international force that would not operate under the banner of the UN, but would instead be commanded and controlled by Trump and his private "Board of Peace"--to which states could buy in for $1 billion and receive permanent membership. In the big picture, Trump could wrap the future edicts of his board in the veneer of UN legitimacy.
As Israel steadily expanded its military attacks on Gaza and pushed its occupation forces deeper into the enclave instead of withdrawing and repositioning them as agreed, Hamas officials told Drop Site that they heard nothing from the Board of Peace until March.
Since then, the negotiations over Gaza's future have been stuck in a diplomatic netherworld. Despite the pomp and circumstance manufactured by the White House after the signing of the deal and Trump's promise to guarantee it, the U.S. has refused to hold Israel to any of its obligations. While Hamas fulfilled its part of the deal and handed over all of its captives to Israel, both alive and dead, Israel has repeatedly violated nearly every term of the agreement and has killed more than 1,000 Palestinians since the signing of the deal in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt.
The talks that have taken place have overwhelmingly centered on attempts by the board to force through changes never agreed to by Palestinians, and effectively transforming a limited ceasefire agreement into a broader political settlement premised on the disarmament of the Palestinian resistance and the abandonment of its national liberation struggle. In a report to the UN Security Council in May, the board called disarming the Palestinian resistance "the single factor that unlocks every other element of the plan." The BoP's proposal, if enacted, would leave Gaza with only a local police force tasked with internal law enforcement and no resistance forces capable of defending Gaza against Israeli occupation or ongoing attacks.
Now, with Western and regional media coverage firmly focused on Iran and the Israeli assault on Lebanon, the current negotiations between Palestinians and the BoP have been almost entirely ignored.
But the Board of Peace is continuing to try to chisel away at any possibility of Palestinian statehood through a 15-point "roadmap" it first presented to Hamas and other Palestinian resistance factions in April. Drop Site News obtained two documents from the latest round of negotiations between the Palestinians and Trump's board. The first is the full text of the Palestinian negotiators' proposed amendments to the board's roadmap for addressing a range of issues, including the demand that Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and their allies submit to total disarmament. The revised document was delivered to the board on June 13. The second document is the response delivered to the Palestinian side last week by Nickolay Mladenov, the BoP's "High Representative."
Taken together, the two versions of the roadmap offer detailed insights into the extent to which Trump's board is trying to erode Palestinian insistence that any long term deal must include a clear path to statehood, that Gaza and the occupied West Bank be treated as a single Palestinian territory, and that the rights of the Palestinian people to resist Israeli occupation and annexation be preserved.
"What we're seeing is an attempt, in the shadow of a genocide, to dismantle the Palestinian resistance through all of these kinds of preconditions," said Abdullah Al-Arian, an associate professor of history at Georgetown University in Qatar. "The interpretation of this agreement is in the hands of actors who are, for the most part, beholden to prioritizing Israel's security."
Mladenov, Bulgaria's former Defense and Foreign Minister, served as UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process from 2015 to 2020. He serves as [director general](https://substack.com/redirect/aec08c35-da1c-4320-b197-a0567228721d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a research academy that trains diplomats from the United Arab Emirates, Israel's closest Arab ally. Until his appointment to Trump's board, Mladenov was also a [visiting fellow](https://substack.com/redirect/f0816b60-f723-47e6-ab59-528105a021d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, a pro-Israel think tank established by veterans of AIPAC.
In some recent negotiations with Hamas, Mladenov has been joined by a senior Trump advisor, Rabbi Aryeh Lightstone, a hardline supporter of Israel who played a key role in the 2020 Abraham Accords.
In their draft, the Palestinian negotiators insist that resolving the issue of weapons can only be addressed as part of a "process that guarantees the Palestinian people's right to establish a Palestinian state and exercise their right to self-determination." The board's draft says only that Palestinian disarmament "shall create conditions for a credible pathway."
The documents also reveal how Trump's board has embraced a decadeslong Israeli tactic of demanding detailed commitments from Palestinians on issues of security and weapons, while offering only vague suggestions of potential Israeli commitments and providing the Palestinian side no substantive recourse when Israel violates the terms.
"Mladenov's latest response reflects the occupation's unwillingness to reach an agreement, despite the movement's compliance with all the demands placed upon it and the significant flexibility it has demonstrated across various issues, including the question of weapons," a senior Hamas official told Drop Site. He requested anonymity because the Palestinian factions have not delivered their official response to Mladenov. "In its current form, this paper is unacceptable and cannot serve as a basis for agreement."
The Board of Peace did not respond to a detailed request for comment on a range of issues.
Hamas officials say the Palestinian factions are currently reviewing Mladenov's reply to their proposed terms. Hazem Qassem, Hamas's spokesperson in Gaza, said the amendments proposed in the Palestinian draft and in a series of recent meetings in Cairo were welcomed by regional mediators from Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey. "The mediators expressed clear satisfaction with the Palestinian factions' responses and viewed them as positive positions that could serve as a foundation for reaching a comprehensive agreement," Qassem said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/2ae5c281-3a9c-4efa-88f7-6a0914d838fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Mladenov continues to approach the file from a perspective close to the Israeli position, a view that was reflected in the proposals he presented during his recent meeting," he argued, saying that Mladenov's attempts to alter terms previously agreed upon with the mediators has "hindered efforts to reach a final agreement."

## **A Framework for Surrender**
Palestinian negotiators have maintained that since the signing of the October agreement, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and board officials, particularly Mladenov, have introduced new conditions that were never part of the original terms, including demands that Palestinian resistance factions relinquish their weapons as a condition for reconstruction to proceed and before Israeli forces complete their withdrawal from the Gaza Strip. In May, Mladenov and Lightstone threatened in a [letter](https://substack.com/redirect/5877f581-366a-4637-b295-68abc681da32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Palestinian officials that if Hamas refuses to capitulate to the disarmament edict, the ceasefire terms would be deemed "null and void," paving the way for Israel to resume its large-scale military operations and halting aid deliveries to Gaza.
"It is clear that Mladenov is conveying the Israeli vision of the agreement and attempting to impose it on us--under the threat of renewed war--the continuation of the current humanitarian catastrophe, and ongoing killings," said the senior Hamas official. "This document is not a framework for an agreement; rather, it is an attempt to impose the surrender that Netanyahu failed to achieve through war."
Israel has committed at least 3,338 ceasefire violations since the October 2025 agreement, according to Palestinian reports shared with mediators and obtained by Drop Site--an average of roughly 13 violations per day. More than 1,000 Palestinians have been killed and over 3,200 wounded in Israeli attacks on Gaza since the agreement entered into force. Israel has also continued to target and assassinate members of the Palestinian resistance, including the commander of Hamas's military wing and his successor within ten days of one another. It has severely restricted the movement of Palestinians and the entry of humanitarian supplies into Gaza, permitting only 36 percent of the agreed quantity of aid to enter the Strip. Israeli forces have also continued expanding the "yellow line" separating the areas they occupy in Gaza further westward. Netanyahu recently pledged to expand Israeli occupation to 70% of Gaza and said the ultimate aim is to conquer the entire territory.
"There's so much that could have been done since October of 2025 to stop Israel. We were, back in October of 2025, the only people in the world that had to negotiate an end to genocide. And here we are now in June of 2026, still negotiating an end to genocide," Diana Buttu, a Palestinian Human Rights lawyer who served as an advisor to the Palestine Liberation Organization during the Oslo negotiations from 2000-2005, told Drop Site. "The amazing thing this time is that it's not even that we're negotiating an end to genocide with the country that's perpetrating genocide. It's that we are now negotiating an end to genocide with a subcontractor."
In public--and in their meetings with Mladenov and other Board officials--Hamas and other Palestinian factions consistently point to the fact that the October 2025 agreement narrowly focused on a ceasefire, exchange of captives, the entry of humanitarian supplies and basic life essentials, and phased Israeli redeployments. Since last October, Hamas negotiators have maintained that they do not have the sole mandate to negotiate on issues that strike at the core of the Palestinian liberation struggle. They argued that discussions over the fate of the weapons held by resistance groups and Gaza's long-term political future must be negotiated with all Palestinian political factions through a democratic process.
Although it was not a requirement of the original text of the ceasefire agreement, Hamas formally agreed to relinquish governing authority in Gaza to the National Committee for Gaza Administration (NCAG), a technocratic committee composed of non-partisan Palestinian experts. Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad formed working groups in Gaza to facilitate the transfer to the NCAG. Israel, however, has blocked the committee from entering Gaza and has falsely claimed the deal mandates that Hamas completely disarm as a condition for the terms of the original deal to be implemented.
"We want to see this administrative committee present in Gaza and carrying out its work there. Everything that needed to be prepared for this committee to function has already been done," Osama Hamdan, a prominent Hamas leader, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/819aa489-2247-4131-8658-7709ad9b1a9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Drop Site in May. He added that Hamas created a mechanism for handing over power, guaranteeing the security of the Committee members, and facilitating them assuming control of the police. "Despite it being formed and approved, Israel still refuses to allow it to enter, and Mladenov has failed to convince the Israelis or compel them."
In the revised document, Mladenov makes the entry of the NCAG into Gaza and the assumption of its duties contingent upon Palestinian acceptance of the "roadmap" and the completion, within 14 days of an agreement, of the second phase's timeline and implementation mechanisms, particularly on Palestinian disarmament.
Israel insists it retains authority to assassinate Palestinian leaders and fighters simply because they are senior members of Hamas or were involved in the October 7 attacks. "I promised that every single architect of the massacre and the hostage-taking would be eliminated down to the last one, and we are very close to completing this mission," Netanyahu proclaimed two days after Israel assassinated Izz Al-Din Al-Haddad, commander of the Qassam Brigades, Hamas's armed wing, on May 15.
Neither Mladenov nor any other board officials have condemned Israel's ongoing assassination of officials from the very party it signed a ceasefire with. Despite Israel's open assassination campaign against Hamas leadership in Gaza, Palestinian resistance factions have continued to respect the terms of the ceasefire.
Although both Hamas and Israel signed the October 2025 document obliging both parties to stop "all military operations, including aerial and artillery bombardment and targeting operations," Mladenov singled out the Palestinian side in his revised document, stating that "Hamas and the Palestinian factions shall immediately cease all military activities."
Instead of holding Israel accountable, Mladenov's public references to ceasefire violations generally avoid any mention of the perpetrator. The ceasefire "is holding in a way that is not perfect. There are violations. Some of them are serious. They mean civilians are still being killed," Mladenov told the UN Security Council in a report on May 26, avoiding mention of Israel, before drawing an equivalence between the October 7 attacks and the subsequent genocide in Gaza that, by conservative estimates, killed more than 80,000 Palestinians.
"At this stage, the principal obstacle to full implementation remains Hamas's refusal to accept verified [weapons] decommissioning, relinquish coercive control, and permit a genuine civilian transition in Gaza," Mladenov added.
A month earlier, on April 19, Mladenov presented Hamas with a 15-point "roadmap" he said was intended to govern the next phase of implementation of a broader deal. While he has publicly described the proposal as a mechanism for stabilization, verification, and institution-building, Palestinian officials contend that it effectively rewrites the terms of the original agreement by conditioning reconstruction, self-governance, and Israeli withdrawal on Palestinian disarmament, while failing to compel Israel to fulfill its first-phase obligations, including ceasing attacks, allowing the agreed quantities of aid into Gaza, fully re-opening the Rafah border crossing, and allowing early reconstruction efforts.
"They've effectively made it so that Palestinian life is only about security for Israel and that's it and nothing else. And it's going to continue to go down this path endlessly," said Buttu. "Even if the [Palestinian] factions signed a blank piece of paper and said, 'Tell us what you want,' the Israelis are still going to be negotiating over that blank piece of paper."

The most consequential issue addressed in the exchanged documents obtained by Drop Site concerns the future of Palestinian weapons. Trump and Netanyahu have falsely claimed that Hamas is violating the deal by not immediately surrendering its weapons and Israel has, at times, cited this as a justification for continuing its attacks against Gaza.
In their June 13 response to Mladenov, Hamas and the Palestinian factions proposed a gradual process for the registration and storage of heavy weapons in parallel with Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and contingent upon the completion of the first phase of the agreement, the entry of the National Committee for Gaza Administration (NCAG), the deployment of the International Stabilization Force (ISF), and the dismantling of Israel-backed armed militias in the Strip. Mladenov's revised text, however, substantially altered both the scope and sequencing of the process.
The Palestinian proposal is limited to "heavy weapons" and focuses on their registration and storage according to an agreed timetable under the joint supervision of the NCAG and Palestinian factions and organizations. Resistance leaders have told Drop Site that Israel is aware that they do not possess powerful weapons and charge that Israel is using the issue of disarmament as a proxy for demanding a public surrender ritual. According to both Israeli and U.S. assessments, the rockets and missile stockpiles of Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad have been largely spent or destroyed during the war.
"There's practically no heavy weapons in Gaza," Netanyahu acknowledged in February. "There's no artillery. There's no tanks. There's nothing." As part of his campaign to entirely strip Palestinians of any weapons that could be used to defend Gaza from Israeli attacks, Netanyahu portrayed assault rifles as the greatest threat. "The heavy weapon, the one that does the most damage, is called an AK-47," he declared. "They did the worst massacre of the Jewish people since the Holocaust with AK-47s."
Senior resistance officials have repeatedly [expressed willingness](https://substack.com/redirect/11864a83-04c5-422c-b434-f1fa88c39135?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to "freeze" and store weapons as part of a long-term truce that would ultimately lead to the establishment of a Palestinian state with its own army.
In its official response to Trump's initiative leading to the October 2025 ceasefire deal, Hamas argued that neither it nor any single faction possesses the authority to negotiate away the weapons of the Palestinian people, maintaining that resistance is a right guaranteed under international law and that any future arrangements concerning weapons must be reached through Palestinian national consensus. "The weapons present in Gaza are primarily weapons of willpower," Mohammed Al-Hindi, the co-founder of Palestinian Islamic Jihad, told Drop Site at the time.
In his response to Hamas last week, however, Mladenov expanded the provision on disarmament into a process to "store and decommission" weapons. His text also broadened the scope beyond heavy weapons to include weapons depots, tunnels, military production facilities, and the weapons stored within them. More significantly, it added a final condition stipulating that, upon completion of the process, Hamas and other Palestinian factions would no longer "hold, store, control or have access to any weapons." The revisions transform the provision from a mechanism governing specific categories of weapons within the context of a long-term truce into a roadmap for the comprehensive dismantlement of Palestinian armed resistance.
These changes become even more significant when read alongside Mladenov's revisions to the provisions governing the International Stabilization Force (ISF), the multi-national troops that would be commanded and overseen by Trump's Board of Peace, and the withdrawal of Israeli forces.
Hamas's draft envisioned the ISF primarily as a buffer force separating Israeli troops from areas administered by the NCAG, monitoring compliance with the ceasefire, and protecting the delivery of life essentials. Mladenov retained those functions but significantly expanded the force's mandate. Although the proposal states that the ISF would not conduct policing operations or engage in matters related to Palestinian society, it simultaneously assigns the force a role in training Palestinian police as well as "support[ing] the decommissioning process." Mladenov's draft does not explain what that support would entail, but several nations that Trump and the Board have sought to enlist as participants in the ISF have explicitly said that they would not participate in a mission to disarm or confront Palestinian resistance forces.
Hamas proposed that Israeli forces withdraw in phases "until they are outside the borders of the Gaza Strip" with the ISF assuming positions in areas vacated by Israeli forces. Hamas said that in parallel to verified stages of Israeli withdrawal, it would implement the agreed upon terms regarding its weapons. Mladenov's response, however, limits Israeli withdrawal only to "Gaza's perimeter" and says it would occur only with "verified progress" in the weapons decommissioning process.
As these negotiations have proceeded, Israel has expanded its occupation of Gaza and has completely bulldozed and razed the area east of the "yellow line" it controls. As Drop Site [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/612a4856-e971-4f00-944d-6788d1069bab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in May, Israel has built and fortified 38 military bases in eastern Gaza, paved roads leading to the bases, and erected 25 kilometers of massive earth berms to physically divide Gaza. From the perspective of Palestinian negotiators, these are not the actions of a party that is planning to withdraw, but the re-establishment of a long-term occupation.

And then who cares about Palestinians in the end?" said Buttu. "They've completely ignored genocide, they've completely ignored the bigger picture of what's happening to the two million people that are in Gaza. And if we don't agree on every single word and every single I that's dotted and T crossed, then Palestinians are just going to continue to starve."
