clean_body: If you've spent a summer in Texas, you know the feeling. ** | | | | | Tuesday, June 23, 2026 Dear Texas Flyover Reader, LMNT has been one of The Flyover's longest-running partners, and that's because it's become a favorite among both our team and our readers. I've used it for years, and it's one of the few products that has remained part of my routine through every season. I was reminded why this past weekend. I spent most of Saturday outside working on a landscaping project in the heat, and by the afternoon I could definitely feel it. I brought along , and it ended up being exactly what I needed. Today, we're sharing more about their newest flavor, plus a free sample pack offer for Texas Flyover readers. -- Cole, CEO If you've spent a summer in Texas, you know the feeling. You walk outside at 8 a.m. and it's already hot. By noon you've been sweating for hours, and by the end of the day you're reaching for another coffee just to keep going. The problem might not be energy. It might be hydration. That's one reason LMNT has become one of The Flyover's longest-running partners. because people use it. Our founder uses it. Our CEO uses it. Members of our team use it. And judging by how often Flyover readers come back and order again, thousands of people in our community do too. Most people know they need water. Fewer realize that hydration depends heavily on electrolytes, especially sodium. In fact, sodium plays a critical role in helping your body absorb and retain the fluids you drink. When you're sweating in the Texas heat, you're losing both water and electrolytes. Replacing one without the other can leave you feeling sluggish, tired, or constantly reaching for another source of caffeine. That's why LMNT was built around a simple idea: more electrolytes, less junk. And now they've introduced something new for summer. LMNT Lemonade Iced Tea combines their electrolyte formula with real tea, 50mg of naturally occurring caffeine, L-Theanine, and beneficial polyphenols. The result is a refreshing iced tea that supports hydration and focus without the overload of many energy drinks and highly caffeinated beverages. One thing we found especially interesting: caffeine doesn't actually create energy. It blocks the receptors that make you feel tired. The real energy production inside your body depends on things like nutrition, hydration, and electrolytes. . Instead of 200, 300, or even 400 milligrams of caffeine, Lemonade Iced Tea delivers a balanced 50mg alongside the electrolytes your body actually needs. For Texans spending weekends on the lake, working outdoors, golfing, traveling, exercising, or simply trying to survive another summer heat wave, it may be worth a look. Right now, Flyover readers can get a FREE LMNT Sample Pack with any purchase. | | The Texas Flyover 448 W 19th St. Suite #356 Houston, TX 77008 | ---|---

I’ve been a practicing OB-GYN for more than 20 years, Peter.
I work hard to meet my patients where they are, listen to their concerns, craft a plan that meets their needs, and provide them with compassionate care informed by the best available evidence.
That’s why I’ve been following this administration’s health policies with consternation and alarm, and I wanted to share some of the things I’m tracking, because this is incredibly important for all of us to be aware of.
→ Earlier this month, it was reported that RFK Jr. is trying to access Americans' private medical records to try to link vaccines with autism. This claim has been exhaustively studied and debunked. And what’s more, the federal government has absolutely no right to access your medical records without your permission, full stop.
→ The FDA has announced they are going to “review the safety” of mifepristone, a drug that has been used safely by millions of women around the world for decades for miscarriage management and to safely end a pregnancy.
→ Hospitals nationwide are battling increasing cases of diseases like measles and whooping cough — diseases that are largely preventable but are making a comeback because of RFK Jr.’s ongoing regurgitation of dangerous disinformation about vaccines.
→ In the wake of the administration withdrawing from the World Health Organization last year, and gutting USAID, RFK Jr. has ordered the lab studying Ebola to halt their research — despite the WHO declaring an Ebola outbreak a global health emergency right now . Infectious diseases don’t respect borders, and Ebola is a dangerous one. The United States should be engaged in this emergency, not pretending it’s not our problem. Global health affects all of us.
All of this is the result of putting someone in charge of public health who doesn't understand medicine or trust science and experts.
I care deeply about public health — as a physician, and as a human. And I will never stop fighting for your right to access safe, science-backed health care.
I’m going to keep standing up against Trump and RFK Jr.’s vision of America from the halls of Congress, and I could really use you by my side.
If you agree that extreme, anti-science ideology has no place in our healthcare system, please chip in to my campaign today so I can hold my seat and help flip the House this fall. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

subject: I’ve studied elections for 50 years. This is a warning.

body:
You need to take this seriously
This is a warning sign. You need to take this seriously

| | | | _**FROM THE DESK OF NEWT GINGRICH**_
---
Peter, I have been studying American elections for over fifty years. I helped engineer the 1994 Republican Revolution that gave us our first House majority in decades. I know what a warning sign looks like. And I am writing to you today because **what is happening in Texas right now is one of the most serious warning signs I have seen in a generation**.

_Let me give you the facts._

A new poll from Texas Public Opinion Research shows Democrat James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 47 to 44 percent in the Texas Senate race. Cook Political Report downgraded the race from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. And Talarico has raised over $40 million for this race, including $27 million in a single quarter, the largest first-quarter fundraising haul ever recorded by a Senate candidate in American history.

Now let me give you the history, because this is where it gets alarming.

**The party that has Majority control almost always loses ground in midterm elections.** It happened to Franklin Roosevelt in 1938. It happened to Lyndon Johnson in 1966. It happened to Bill Clinton in 1994. It happened to Barack Obama in 2010. And frankly, it happened to us in 2018. The American electorate has a long and consistent pattern of using the midterm election to push back against the party in power, and anyone who tells you 2026 will be different is not being honest with you.

The Democrats know this history better than anyone. They are running and fully supporting James Talarico in Texas because they have looked at the historical map, seen the midterm pattern, calculated the fundraising numbers, and decided that Texas is winnable. And right now, the polling and the money say they may be correct.

Here is what makes this moment even more critical. Talarico had no runoff. He spent three months doing nothing but raising money and organizing for the general election. He started the general election campaign with a three-month head start, a 3-point lead, and a $38 million fundraising advantage.

**_I have seen what happens when Republicans ignore these early warning signs. I have also seen what happens when we take them seriously and fight back._**

In 1994 we took them seriously. We organized. We raised the money. We delivered a message that resonated with the American people. And we won.

You need to take this seriously | | | | FROM THE DESK OF NEWT GINGRICH Peter, I have been studying American elections for over fifty years. I helped engineer the 1994 Republican Revolution that gave us our first House majority in decades. I know what a warning sign looks like. And I am writing to you today because what is happening in Texas right now is one of the most serious warning signs I have seen in a generation. Let me give you the facts. A new poll from Texas Public Opinion Research shows Democrat James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 47 to 44 percent in the Texas Senate race. Cook Political Report downgraded the race from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. And Talarico has raised over $40 million for this race, including $27 million in a single quarter, the largest first-quarter fundraising haul ever recorded by a Senate candidate in American history. Now let me give you the history, because this is where it gets alarming. The party that has Majority control almost always loses ground in midterm elections. It happened to Franklin Roosevelt in 1938. It happened to Lyndon Johnson in 1966. It happened to Bill Clinton in 1994. It happened to Barack Obama in 2010. And frankly, it happened to us in 2018. The American electorate has a long and consistent pattern of using the midterm election to push back against the party in power, and anyone who tells you 2026 will be different is not being honest with you. The Democrats know this history better than anyone. They are running and fully supporting James Talarico in Texas because they have looked at the historical map, seen the midterm pattern, calculated the fundraising numbers, and decided that Texas is winnable. And right now, the polling and the money say they may be correct. Here is what makes this moment even more critical. Talarico had no runoff. He spent three months doing nothing but raising money and organizing for the general election. He started the general election campaign with a three-month head start, a 3-point lead, and a $38 million fundraising advantage. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | President Trump — a sweeping change that could forever alter retirement accounts, including millions of 401(k)s. body:

DEVELOPING... In a last-minute maneuver, Sen. Mike Lee brazenly added an amendment
to repeal the Roadless Area Conservation Rule to a bipartisan bill about
wildfire prevention. He did this right beforeit passed a key Senate committee on an 11-9 partisan vote. Now, it moves on to
the full Senate. Lee’s amendment would overturn protections against logging and industrial
road-building on 45 million acres of national forests. We can’t let this stand, Peter— LCV is mobilizing immediately, but taking on MAGA politicians and corporate
polluters who stand to turn a profit by repealing the Roadless Rule takes
resources. We need to move fast and keep the pressure on Congress high. So,
we’re asking: Will you renew your LCV membership for just $15 today to power our work to stop this amendment before it becomes law and defend our national forests? The first 5,000 contributions to our Summer Membership Drive will be TRIPLE MATCHED to protect public lands >> https://links.messages.lcv. PROTECT OUR FORESTS: RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv. The Roadless Rule protects pristine national forest lands from road
construction, logging, and development that would forever alter these important
ecosystems. Keeping these unspoiled landscapes protected requires constant
vigilance, but this amendment to the Wildfire Prevention Act is all about
stripping these landscapes of protections to sell off our public lands to
destructive corporations. If Senator Lee’s amendment passes with the rest of the bill, the consequences
for our forests could be catastrophic, including higher wildfire risk due to increased human and industrial activity. LCV 2026 SUMMER MEMBERSHIP DRIVE Goal: 5,000 members

Deadline: June 30, 2026

Match offer: First 5,000 contributions will be TRIPLED

Renew your membership now to claim your triple match >> https://links.messages.lcv. Let’s call this what it is: a cynical, bad-faith attempt to sneak a repeal of
the Roadless Rule into a piece of bipartisan legislation, without debate or a
standalone vote.Pro-polluter politicians like Mike Lee know their plans to sell out our national
forests won’t pass on their own merits, so they have to use gambits like this to
try to get their way. We’re working with lawmakers, partners, and grassroots activists across the
country to prevent this amendment from becoming law, but we need your help. Please don’t sit this one out, Peter: renew your LCV membership for $15 today and if you’re one of the first 5,000 donors to our Summer Membership Drive, your contribution will be TRIPLED to defend our forests >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/04wrM8K_ Thank you for responding when our national forests need you. name: Wes Moore
subject: One last message to you before polls close in Maryland…
body:
Today is Primary Election Day in Maryland.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1536%2E1086043%2EydzaJn)
[ ](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260623-1.H_ncAu&refcode=em-20260623-1&t=2&akid=1536%2E1086043%2EydzaJn)
This is it, Peter.
**Today is Primary Election Day in Maryland, so I’m asking one final time before polls close tonight:**
**[Can I count on you to support my campaign for re-election?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260623-1.H_ncAu&refcode=em-20260623-1&t=3&akid=1536%2E1086043%2EydzaJn)**
Once every last vote is counted, we’ll find out who our Republican opponent will be in the general election. The race to determine the next chapter of the state of Maryland will officially begin.
Here’s what we already know: the general election will bring on new challenges for our campaign. Attacks on me from our opponents will ramp up quickly, and the MAGA forces who want to see us fail will throw everything they’ve got at this race.
But after tonight, we’ll also face new opportunities. Together, we will have the chance to prove that Maryland is ready to keep fighting for progress, and that we are determined to keep building on the results we’ve delivered to make Maryland more affordable for families.
I am incredibly proud of all that we’ve accomplished together, Peter. **Now, with just hours until polls close tonight, I need you by my side as we run through the tape.**
**[Will you donate $5 – or any amount that feels right to you – to fuel our campaign as we officially enter the general election after tonight? We’ll need every ounce of support to win re-election and hold on to this crucial governor’s seat in Maryland.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260623-1.H_ncAu&refcode=em-20260623-1&t=4&akid=1536%2E1086043%2EydzaJn)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260623-1.H_ncAu&amount=5&refcode=em-20260623-1&t=23&akid=1536%2E1086043%2EydzaJn)**
To you, and to every person who’s believed in our people-powered campaign, I want to say _thank you._ Let’s do this!
Elevate,
Wes

* * *
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-footer?refcode=em-20260623-1&t=24&refcode2=1536_1086043_ydzaJn&akid=1536%2E1086043%2EydzaJn)**
**[Volunteer »](https://support.wesmoore.com/a/volunteer?source=em-20260623-1)**

In 2024, I ran for Congress in Maryland. I fought as hard as I knew how. I knocked on doors, made calls, and connected with voters.
The voters who heard my message? They were with me.
_The problem was getting heard at all._
Dark money donors spent MILLIONS of dollars to drown me out, and it worked. I watched it happen in real time — ads I couldn't match, mailers I couldn't answer, and a wall of money between me and the voters I was trying to reach.
When you have that kind of money, you don't have to win the argument. You just have to make sure the other side can't be heard.
I could've walked away. God knows it would've been easier.
But I filed to run again.
**I stood inside the United States Capitol on January 6th and watched Donald Trump's mob try to tear our democracy apart with their bare hands. I held the line that day. I testified. I fought back with everything I had.**
And I'll be damned if I let dark money and MAGA intimidation knock me down.
I'm running for this district, for this state, and for the idea that our democracy is worth defending even when it's hard. Especially when it's hard.
That means standing up to Donald Trump. It means standing up to the billionaires and the PACs and the anonymous money that's quietly buying our elections out from under us.

body:
Dan Goldman for New York [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/94087/images/Logo-White-BG.png]
Peter,

In Trump’s nosediving economy, Americans are increasingly being forced to use Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) loans to cover basic expenses. As we know, that short-term solution creates even greater long-term financial risk.

That’s why I just introduced legislation — the Buy Now Pay Later Consumer Protection Act — to fix that.

BNPL loans lack the same protections as credit cards, including clear fee disclosures, dispute rights, and refunds for canceled services. BNPL usage can be catastrophic for users’ personal finances and credit scores. My bill will protect buyers, crack down on BNPL rip-offs, and help keep money in Americans’ pockets.

These short-term loans allow people to make a purchase and pay it off in multiple interest-free payments. But if they miss or are late on a payment, they can be charged late fees, bounce payment fees, and other hidden fees, which can add up to the equivalent of a high annual percentage rate.

My legislation would require BNPL companies to:

* Provide clear disclosures about fees and pricing.
* Provide periodic statements showing charges made, fees, payments and credits applied, amounts due, and due dates, as well as where to send billing disputes.
* Provide time after a statement is delivered to the consumer to pay before late fees or negative credit reporting.
* Provide dispute rights such as the right to get a refund for returned items, the right to challenge billing errors or improper charges, and the right not to be held liable for unauthorized uses.

The deck is already stacked against working families in Trump’s economy. I will keep fighting for them and against the special interests trying to exploit them.

Please sign on as a citizen cosponsor to help show the scale of public support and push this bill forward. [https://action.dangoldmanforny.com/a/pet-202606-buy-now-pay-later]

subject: Our democracy just suffered a blow. But the fight continues.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
There’s no way to sugarcoat this: A federal judge just refused to block Donald Trump’s executive order to create a federal voter list and limit mail voting.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
That means the fight to protect free, fair, and accessible elections just suffered a blow — and the stakes could not be higher.
Trump and his allies are still trying to sow distrust in our elections, restrict access to the ballot box, and give the federal government unprecedented control over how Americans vote. They’re targeting vote-by-mail even after repeated audits and investigations confirmed there was no widespread fraud in the 2020 election.
And make no mistake: this is exactly why we need everyone on board, fighting back harder than ever to save our democracy and the rule of law.
In Oregon, we know vote-by-mail works. We’ve spent decades building a system that is secure, accessible, and trusted by voters across the political spectrum. But national attacks on voting rights don’t stop at state borders.
As Secretary of State, I’ll do everything in my power to protect Oregon voters, defend election workers from political intimidation, and ensure our elections remain free from partisan interference.
But I can’t do this alone. We to prove that Oregonians are ready to stand together against these attacks on democracy. Will you chip in before midnight to help me continue this fight? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
The courts may not have stopped this latest attack yet — but voting rights advocates are continuing the legal battle, and we must continue organizing, mobilizing, and preparing for what comes next.
This campaign is about protecting democracy itself. And it will take all of us working together to win.
Thank you,
Tobias Read

| Yesterday, I told you we expected new attacks against our campaign as we entered the final week of this race.
And unsurprisingly, here they come.
New xenophobic ads just went on the air questioning my ties to Denver. These ads go so far as to say I'm just "not Denver" despite the fact that I immigrated here with my parents as an infant!
But listen, I wouldn't be running for Congress if I didn't have thick skin.
I'm not worried about what a bunch of Washington consultants running cringey ads have to say about me and my relationship to the place I call home.
But it does make me wonder about my opponent Diana DeGette...
How are you supposed to take on ICE when the people on your side are running ads that say immigrants need not apply.
Hmm...
I got into this race because I love Denver. I love our neighborhoods, families, diversity, and our deep belief that everyone deserves a place to belong.
And I will fight anyone who tries to play gatekeeper over who is and isn't part of this city. That includes ICE, racist Super PACs, and politicians who take contributions from ICE contractors while getting a little too cozy with their language.
So if you're in a position to give, please donate today to help us drown out this garbage.

clean_body: We're taking on the corporate Democratic establishment in Colorado as we fight for Medicare for All, workers’ rights, and making the wealthiest people in our country pay their fair share. | | | Peter, Working Families champions across the country are winning big this primary season — with recent sweeps in California, Georgia, and DC showing that voters are ready for bold, people-powered candidates to send status-quo incumbents packing. Next up? Colorado, where in just one week, Julie Gonzales and Melat Kiros are on the ballot — along with dozens of other WFP candidates — to fight for the policies working families need. Julie Gonzales’s campaign for Senate and Melat Kiros’s campaign for Colorado’s 1st Congressional District are taking on the corporate Democratic establishment in fighting for Medicare for All, workers’ rights, and making the wealthiest people in our country pay their fair share. Julie Gonzales, a community organizer, state senator, and founding member of the COWFP, is running against Sen. John Hickenlooper — who describes himself as a “fiscal conservative” and voted to confirm nearly half of Trump’s cabinet nominees. As a Senator, Julie would fiercely oppose Trump’s authoritarian administration, take on price-gouging tech CEOs, and fight to make our communities affordable for working families. Melat Kiros is running against Rep. Diana DeGette, who has taken almost $5.5 million from corporate PACs since joining Congress in 1997, primarily from pharmaceutical companies and the healthcare industry. Melat refuses to take any corporate PAC money as she fights for housing reform, consumer protections, universal healthcare, and more. These two champions would be invaluable voices in the House and Senate as we build a coalition of WFP champions that will make the Working Families Guarantee a reality: A home you can afford, healthcare you can rely on, a good union job, affordable childcare, and paid family leave — paid for by making the wealthy pay their fair share and getting big money out of politics. | | Hi Friend,

I’ve spent 30 years organizing in the Bay – alongside young women navigating poverty, families fighting to remain housed, and communities demanding safety.

That work taught me to recognize when leaders are in this fight to help the people around them, not themselves.

**That’s how I know that Randy Villegas is the real deal.**

At 31, Randy is exactly the kind of leader the Central Valley needs. He’s the son of working-class Mexican immigrants, an educator, an auto shop owner, a school board trustee, and a dedicated fighter for working families who doesn’t take a single penny of corporate PAC money.

clean_body: We're taking on the corporate Democratic establishment in Colorado as we fight for Medicare for All, workers’ rights, and making the wealthiest people in our country pay their fair share. | | | Peter, Working Families champions across the country are winning big this primary season — with recent sweeps in California, Georgia, and DC showing that voters are ready for bold, people-powered candidates to send status-quo incumbents packing. Next up? Colorado, where in just one week, Julie Gonzales and Melat Kiros are on the ballot — along with dozens of other WFP candidates — to fight for the policies working families need. Julie Gonzales’s campaign for Senate and Melat Kiros’s campaign for Colorado’s 1st Congressional District are taking on the corporate Democratic establishment in fighting for Medicare for All, workers’ rights, and making the wealthiest people in our country pay their fair share. Julie Gonzales, a community organizer, state senator, and founding member of the COWFP, is running against Sen. John Hickenlooper — who describes himself as a “fiscal conservative” and voted to confirm nearly half of Trump’s cabinet nominees. As a Senator, Julie would fiercely oppose Trump’s authoritarian administration, take on price-gouging tech CEOs, and fight to make our communities affordable for working families. Melat Kiros is running against Rep. Diana DeGette, who has taken almost $5.5 million from corporate PACs since joining Congress in 1997, primarily from pharmaceutical companies and the healthcare industry. Melat refuses to take any corporate PAC money as she fights for housing reform, consumer protections, universal healthcare, and more. These two champions would be invaluable voices in the House and Senate as we build a coalition of WFP champions that will make the Working Families Guarantee a reality: A home you can afford, healthcare you can rely on, a good union job, affordable childcare, and paid family leave — paid for by making the wealthy pay their fair share and getting big money out of politics. body:
An independent judge just rejected Trump’s politically motivated investigation into me.
#
Breaking news, Peter:
Yesterday, a federal judge rejected the U.S. Department of Justice’s politically motivated investigation into me.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260623-1.RNI2RA&amount=5&refcode=em20260623-785&t=2&akid=785%2E34582%2Eh9Flju)
Let me be clear about what happened here: **Donald Trump tried to use the DOJ as his personal revenge factory.**
He ordered a criminal investigation into a political opponent. It was unconstitutional. It was meritless. And today, a federal judge saw it for exactly what it was.
This is not how America is supposed to work. The Department of Justice does not belong to Donald Trump. It does not exist to intimidate his opponents, punish people who stand up to him, or scare Democrats into silence.
But that is exactly what Trump wants. He wants us looking over our shoulders. He wants us afraid to fight back. He wants anyone who challenges him to wonder if they will be next.
**Let me be clear: I won’t be intimidated. And I don’t think you will be either.**
**[So today, I’m asking you to stand with me. Will you make a contribution of $5 now to show Trump, his allies, and every MAGA politician trying to weaponize power against their opponents that we will not back down?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260623-1.RNI2RA&amount=5&refcode=em20260623-785&t=3&akid=785%2E34582%2Eh9Flju)**

Thank you for having my back.
– Tim Walz

name: David Hogg
subject: Elon Musk is officially a trillionaire
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
This should be a wake up call.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260623-1&t=1&akid=3631%2E587540%2EKatg82)
Peter, you might have seen the news that Elon Musk is officially a trillionaire.
Yeah, that’s not a typo. _Trillionaire._
The fact that the richest man in the world is only getting richer — and he’s an extreme right-wing ideologue — should be a serious wake up call for all of us.
As a result of the Supreme Court's _Citizens United_ decision, Elon Musk can pour as much of his fortune as he wants into our elections. The Court calls that "free speech."
In 2024, Musk spent over **$277 million** supporting Trump and MAGA Republicans.
**So let me ask: do you and Elon Musk have an equal say in our government?**
_I know I don't._
It's time to fix a broken system. One that lets a trillionaire pay a smaller share of his income in taxes than a teacher, and lets a man like Musk buy off the very people sworn to protect us.
Elon spending hundreds of millions on elections is not free speech, it's legalized bribery.
In 2026, Elon has even more money to spend on bankrolling his chosen candidates. And I can guarantee you that none of those candidates are good for our country.
_But here’s the good news:_ Leaders We Deserve doesn’t need a trillion dollars to fight back. We’re already on an incredible winning streak, and we aren’t done. We’ve endorsed double the number of candidates we did in 2024. We aren’t messing around here. _We’re electing the young progressive leaders we deserve._
At Leaders We Deserve, we’re laying the groundwork and taking a generational bet to fix this broken system using the people who have the most to lose: young Americans.
**I don’t have to remind you that we don’t have Elon Musk and his uber-wealthy buddies behind us. But we’re much more proud of the fact that we have _YOU_.**
Grassroots supporters have funded every major victory Leaders We Deserve has achieved so far. And that’s exactly who we’ll be standing with in every single race.
**[Will you pitch in $5 or anything you can now to keep powering this fight?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260623_1_elon.9GjP_n&refcode=em20260623-3631&amount=5&t=2&akid=3631%2E587540%2EKatg82)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

name: Gov. Madeleine Kunin
subject: Why I’m Supporting Molly Gray for Lt. Gov.
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]
Dear Peter,
When I was elected Vermont’s lieutenant governor in 1978, I became only the second woman to hold the office. Since then, I’ve served as Vermont’s first woman governor, Deputy U.S. Secretary of Education, and U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland.
But today, I want to talk about why the office of lieutenant governor matters.
In 1979, the Vermont Senate was deadlocked 15–15 over an amendment that would have restricted funding for Planned Parenthood and limited access to reproductive health care in our state. As lieutenant governor, one of my responsibilities was to preside over the Senate and cast tie-breaking votes.
When that moment came, I voted against the restriction. My vote ensured that access to abortion care remained protected and that Vermont women did not lose fundamental rights.
That experience taught me an important lesson: the office of lieutenant governor is not ceremonial. It carries real power, and who holds it can have a profound impact on the lives of Vermonters.
That is why I am supporting Molly Gray.
Molly has spent her career fighting for human rights and public service—as a human rights lawyer and advocate, a former Vermont Assistant Attorney General, and as lieutenant governor. Since then, she has continued serving Vermonters by leading a statewide effort to help Afghan refugees resettle in Vermont. She has also become a mother and remains a strong advocate for working families.
I know Molly. I trust her judgment, her values, and her commitment to protecting the rights and freedoms of Vermonters. She understands both the responsibility and the potential of this office, and she has the experience, determination, and courage to lead during challenging times.
We need to help send her back to the lieutenant governor’s office.
Will you join me by making a contribution today?

**[From peer-review scandal to cultural warning: Dr. James Lindsay comes to Freedom Fest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
James Lindsay voted for Democrats into his thirties. He will tell you that himself, and he’ll tell you exactly why. He knew he disliked George W. Bush. He knew Bush was a Republican. The other side, he figured, must be better.
“That was the depth of my political analysis right there,” Lindsay said. He means it as a confession, not a punchline.
He was, at the time, a mathematician with a PhD from the University of Tennessee, living in Maryville in the foothills of the Smokies, running a business that fused martial arts and massage therapy. Not exactly the profile of someone who would end up warning the European Parliament about the collapse of Western civilization. But that was before a peer reviewer’s note about a single word in a paper changed the course of his life.
Lindsay speaks at the RMV Freedom Fest on Saturday, June 27, at the Douglas County Fairgrounds in Castle Rock. His session is titled “Exposing Critical Theory in Plain English.” For those who have followed his work, the subject is familiar. For those who haven’t, the story of how he got there is worth knowing.

**[Colorado’s main suer runs on Trump](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY TOM ANTHONY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Weiser has built his campaign almost entirely on anti-Trump litigation:** the author argues that with $2 trillion in annual federal medical costs growing at nearly double digits and Colorado facing real fiscal pressures, spending taxpayer resources on 66 lawsuits against a political opponent leaves nothing left to address the problems ordinary Coloradans actually face.
* **Weiser's record on energy reveals where his loyalties lie:** when the Department of Energy ordered the coal-fired Craig Unit 1 in Moffat County to stay open, Weiser fought to let it retire — choosing the state's climate agenda over a plant tied to 47 percent of the county's GDP in a community that gave Trump 81 percent of its vote.
* **The author contrasts Weiser with RFK Jr., who spent 20 years defending people against pharmaceutical industry corruption:** while Weiser as a Democrat must "pander to the medical industry," the commentary argues the real reform impulse on healthcare now sits with Trump's appointees, not Colorado's litigator-in-chief.

We held hands, spun in circles, laughed, and then intentionally fell to the ground together. Nobody was trying to win. Nobody was competing for attention. Nobody was demanding their rights. For a few brief moments, everyone moved together...Then we grew up!_
**[What our fathers taught us](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | COMMENTARY | JUNE 21** _We put a single question to some of the writers you read here: what’s the best thing your father taught you, or the thing you didn’t understand until much later? Nobody sent us a speech. They sent us a memory. Some are about work. Some are about faith, or grit, or a sentence a man said once and never repeated. Much of what these dads handed down came through more than instruction. Your father taught you most in ways he probably didn’t plan. Most of us figure that out later._ __

name: Adam Dunigan
subject: Adam Dunigan Event Invitations!
body:
A list of events for anyone curious to meet Adam, the Marine Corps veteran and ex-CIA heartthrob stealing America's heart in Virginia's 8th District.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/CDBIBshk3mP?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)
| | | | | | Hey friends, it’s Adam Dunigan. I have been very poor about getting these newsletter updates out, I know. Turns out campaigning is exactly as chaotic as everyone said it would be. But I’m here now! In your inbox and in your heart (hopefully).
We’ve got our first debate this weekend. That’s pretty exciting. Wish me luck up there, and if you’re in the Northern Virginia area, come attend. We’ve also got a couple very cool opportunities to come out and hang with me and the team over the next few days. Details are below for each day’s activities.
**Upcoming Events**
* **Wednesday, June 24th** \- 7:30PM, World Cup - Mexico game at Alexandria Bier Garden. Featuring participation from Amanda Nelson from [@AmandasMildTakes](https://us.list-manage.com/L6vStLYk1CB?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) and another _secret surprise guest_. Reveal will be day-of. No sign up necessary, just come grab a Bier but do NOT grab the Garden, they get upset when you do that.
* **Thursday, June 25th** \- 7PM, The Back House Studio in Falls Church (6066 Leesburg Pike, Suite 540). Come hang out with the Back House Studio Crew for an informal Town Hall/Q+A. Jordan, Ceci, and the rest of the Back House crew always do it up real nice. Wine and snacks provided. No sign up necessary, just believe in yourself.
* **Saturday, June 27th** \- 6PM, “Celebrating the Human Spirit” in Crystal City. Location disclosed once you [register to attend](https://us.list-manage.com/OBJQ6YKkwpD?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0). This is a big one, and I’m really hoping we get a good crowd, so please consider attending.
* The evening will be catered by our friends at Inca Social and feature performances from Iranian-American activist and the world’s only female ambidextrous violinist [Vienna Lionheart](https://us.list-manage.com/6o34FFkWyll?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0). Vienna’s story of escaping oppression in Iran is inspirational, and you will want to be there to hear it.
* The event is also honoring the memory of artist and USAID officer Joe Connors, and will feature a silent auction of some of his art pieces. Our host for the evening will be Anne Ralte, Joe’s widow and herself a casualty of the DOGE purges and destruction of USAID.
* These are good people, and I’m honored by their support. Even if you don’t want to meet me, come meet them.
* **Sunday, June 28th** \- 3PM, FCDC Virginia’s 8th District Candidate Debate! Franconia Government Center in Alexandria. [Register here.](https://us.list-manage.com/MNcH8jD559I?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) This is the first debate! I’m nervous as hell! Please come attend if you can, and help me through my stage fright. Honestly, the conversation should be illuminating. This is the first time all the VA08 candidates will share the same space, so could be a disaster or it could be great. Let’s see! Unpredictability is the spice of life! And if I am one thing...

That’s the update for the latter half of this week. Hope to see y’all out there. As always, if you can, [please consider donating to the campaign](https://us.list-manage.com/spTWjBkF0Rm?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) so I can pay my team a fair wage, get our message out there effectively, and afford both lunch AND dinner. On the same day! I know! Luxurious.
We’re in the home stretch ahead of August 4th. Every little bit helps. Appreciate you all, and feel free to hit me with any questions. I’m here for it.
Adam Duniganwww.Adam4Congress.com

Thursday, June 25th \- 7PM, The Back House Studio in Falls Church (6066 Leesburg Pike, Suite 540). Come hang out with the Back House Studio Crew for an informal Town Hall/Q+A. Jordan, Ceci, and the rest of the Back House crew always do it up real nice. Wine and snacks provided. No sign up necessary, just believe in yourself. Saturday, June 27th \- 6PM, “Celebrating the Human Spirit” in Crystal City. Location disclosed once you . This is a big one, and I’m really hoping we get a good crowd, so please consider attending. The evening will be catered by our friends at Inca Social and feature performances from Iranian-American activist and the world’s only female ambidextrous violinist . Vienna’s story of escaping oppression in Iran is inspirational, and you will want to be there to hear it. The event is also honoring the memory of artist and USAID officer Joe Connors, and will feature a silent auction of some of his art pieces. Our host for the evening will be Anne Ralte, Joe’s widow and herself a casualty of the DOGE purges and destruction of USAID. These are good people, and I’m honored by their support. Even if you don’t want to meet me, come meet them. Sunday, June 28th \- 3PM, FCDC Virginia’s 8th District Candidate Debate! Franconia Government Center in Alexandria. This is the first debate! I’m nervous as hell! Please come attend if you can, and help me through my stage fright. Honestly, the conversation should be illuminating. This is the first time all the VA08 candidates will share the same space, so could be a disaster or it could be great. Let’s see! Unpredictability is the spice of life! And if I am one thing... That’s the update for the latter half of this week. Hope to see y’all out there. As always, if you can, so I can pay my team a fair wage, get our message out there effectively, and afford both lunch AND dinner. On the same day! I know! Luxurious. We’re in the home stretch ahead of August 4th. Every little bit helps. Appreciate you all, and feel free to hit me with any questions. I’m here for it. body:
The headlines may have faded. The cameras may have moved on. But the bad news is that many January 6 defendants still need your help.
---
[View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e7382884/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvdEo3M3RGWkpFRg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA2MjM/LbmNsMURvaDRSRw/qP2hpZHM9bmNsNEdGOVE0YzZRQXZscw/gajrdlA/s7u207122da)

[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
Patriot,

The headlines may have faded. The cameras may have moved on. But the bad news is that many January 6 defendants still need your help.

For countless American patriots and their families, the consequences of January 6 continue. Many lost their jobs. Many depleted their savings. Some returned home to overwhelming debt, damaged credit, broken careers, and families struggling to make ends meet.

The challenges didn't end when they walked out of prison or returned home.

In many cases, that's when a new battle began...

But I have good news: Stand in the Gap created the Lifeline Fund to do something about it.

**The Lifeline Fund exists to provide immediate relief for former January 6 defendants and their families as they work to rebuild their lives.**

Whether it's helping cover rent, utilities, vehicle expenses, emergency bills, or other urgent needs, this program serves as a critical safety net for families facing difficult circumstances.

**Today, I'm asking for your support because the need is growing, and our resources must grow with it.**

Our goal is to raise $60,000 in the next 60 days to ensure we can continue providing lifesaving assistance to the patriots who need it most.

[Will you make a donation of any amount to the Lifeline Fund today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate $10](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $35](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $50](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $100](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $250](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $1,000](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate Any Amount](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
The reality is simple: financial instability makes rebuilding nearly impossible.

When a family is worried about keeping the lights on, making a mortgage payment, or finding reliable transportation to get to work, it's difficult to focus on healing and moving forward.

**The Lifeline Fund helps relieve those immediate burdens so families can focus on creating a better future.**

* We've been able to provide emergency assistance when families had nowhere else to turn.
* We've helped cover essential expenses during moments of crisis.
* We've connected generous donors with individuals in need of transportation and other critical resources.

The Lifeline Fund is dedicated to easing the financial and emotional burdens faced by former January 6 defendants and their families as they navigate the challenges of reintegration.

But there are many more people waiting for help.

And that's why your support today matters so much.

[You can offer immediate, practical relief for January 6 defendants in need by donating today.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
When you support the Lifeline Fund, you're doing more than paying a bill or covering an expense.

You are making sure that no patriot faces these challenges alone.

You're reminding someone that they haven't been forgotten. You're helping restore dignity. You're providing breathing room during an incredibly difficult chapter of life.

**Most importantly, you're standing shoulder-to-shoulder with fellow Americans who need their community now more than ever.**

We have just 60 days to raise $60,000 for the Lifeline Fund.

Every contribution helps provide emergency assistance, housing support, transportation, and other critical needs for former January 6 defendants and their families.

[Please make your donation today and help us reach this important goal. >>](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $1,000](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate Any Amount](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
Thank you for standing in the gap when others cannot.

For Freedom,

Shane Jenkins
Founder and Executive Director of Stand in the Gap

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/09a3f776-0d30-429d-bbbe-7e40084b6995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**by David Shuster**_
One of Donald Trump's defining characteristics is that he repeatedly enters situations he does not understand, dismisses expert advice, and leaves behind a larger mess than the one he wants to fix. Or, as social media describes it, everything Trump touches turns to shit.
It is now clear there is a pattern and consistency with Trump's Presidential defecations, whether it's a public works project like the now green Lincoln memorial reflecting pool or the economic implosion thanks the disastrous military confrontation with Iran.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/09a3f776-0d30-429d-bbbe-7e40084b6995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The comparison may seem odd at first. What could a reflecting pool and a Middle Eastern war possibly have in common? The answer is narcissism fueled decision-making.
Fixing or improving a public works project requires careful planning, engineering expertise, environmental analysis, and an understanding of basic science. Just because Trump wants the water to look like it's in a gigantic blue swimming pool doesn't mean the water will simply obey.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Ej8aHX54daPNdgvtRMPIcU7UZF4dMV0E3_29w_nCAYk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=203152308)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/09a3f776-0d30-429d-bbbe-7e40084b6995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The same principles apply to foreign policy.
Iran is not a casino in Atlantic City that can be rebranded with a new sign. It is not a Manhattan building where a flashy lobby can distract from structural flaws. It is a nation of nearly ninety million people sitting at the center of one of the world's most volatile regions. Every military action sets off consequences, including economic fallout, that can spread far beyond the first explosion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/09a3f776-0d30-429d-bbbe-7e40084b6995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But consequences have never been Trump's strong suit.
Again and again, Trump has approached complex problems as though they are simple matters of willpower. Reflecting pool experts warned of complications in simply painting the bottom blue. They asked, "what about fixing the leaky connection pipes that fuel algae growth?" "No," Trump insisted. "Just get me the blue by July 4 and spend whatever it takes."
$13 million dollars later, following a no-bid contract to a Trump friend, the Lincoln memorial reflecting pool has splotchy green patches and is more awful looking than ever.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=203152308&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAzMTUyMzA4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODIyNDM4NTgsImV4cCI6MTc4NDgzNTg1OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.TB5hRDOensXUuUc6q2EtNLun5skDhCJZzhxZE4BceRc)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/09a3f776-0d30-429d-bbbe-7e40084b6995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In considering Iran, U.S. diplomats and military planners warned Trump of potential problems in the Persian Gulf. They said Iran might respond to war by closing the Strait of Hormuz. Trump turned away the caution with a simple, "no, I don't think so." And now, with ships still bottled up in the Strait, world oil supplies are weeks away from being exhausted and gas prices in the U.S. are headed towards $5/gallon.
Trump's Operation Epic Surrender, as Senate Republicans are calling his effort to end the war, includes immediately unfreezing hundreds of millions of dollars of Iranian assets. Trump has also promised the Iranian regime that the U.S. will secure $300B in reconstruction investments. And there is still no agreement on Iran's nuclear ambitions.

Like so many of you, I’ve been worried about the corruption and division emanating from Washington. We need fighters who are going to bring people together and stand up for our democracy and our communities.
That’s who John Hickenlooper is.
John’s not a typical politician. He was a laid-off geologist who took a chance and opened Denver's very first brewpub, Wynkoop Brewing Company – a place where people with different perspectives and backgrounds come together, enjoy one another’s presence, and talk through differences and common ground. He understands the importance of engaging other people, not through the lens of ideology, but as human beings with shared interests and values.
That’s exactly what he’s done as a public servant. As governor, he expanded Medicaid to 500,000 Coloradans. And in the Senate, he negotiated the largest effort to fight climate change in our nation’s history. He helped pass the most consequential housing bill in decades to make life more affordable. And I turned to him often in our work to deliver historic investments to fix America’s aging infrastructure.
Time and again, John has proven he’s committed to making Colorado a great place to call home.
And, John certainly didn’t give up when the president targeted Colorado. He helped stop Trump’s slush fund for criminals. He defeated MAGA’s plan to sell off our public lands. He’s fought to protect Americans' health care and lower prices after Trump’s outrageous budget bill gutted funding for our health care system to give tax cuts to his rich friends.
That’s what I admire most about John. At a time when other people thought about giving up, John refused to back down. He’s focused on what matters most – fighting for working families.

clean_body: Peter, We knew the attacks on our democracy would escalate when Trump reentered office last year, but what we are seeing right now is a terrifying new low. ICE agents are going to local election officials to demand individual voter files. Trump’s push to manufacture a crisis around noncitizen voting has evolved into a dangerous, multi-agency effort reaching directly into state and local voter systems. This isn't about election integrity;it’s a coordinated strategy to terrorize our communities and discourage voters of color from showing up to the polls. They’re trying to turn our right to vote into a legal minefield to scare eligible Latino voters into staying home. But we refuse to back down. We are on the ground ensuring our communities are registered, informed, and ready to assert their civic power at the ballot box. They are changing the rules to dilute our power, but we know our rights, and we will not be erased. Thank you, Voto Latino

Justice PAC and my campaign because a new poll just showed me leading my
opponent by 5 points in this toss-up race for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat.

If you’ve already seen the new poll and understand why I need your support
to continue scaling up our campaign across the Last Frontier, please use
this link to split a donation:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260623-split.U7dtFf&refcode=em20260623-61570&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=61570%2E1407376%2EDH-wuj ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dj-em-20260623-split

This poll is a testament to our support across Alaska, and I am so
energized by the movement we’re building. Together, we are creating a
historic effort to fight for our future and to take on the DC
establishment and corporate special interests.

But it also reveals a concerning trend.

Last month, polling showed that our lead was cut in half. And we haven’t
made up that ground since.

My opponent and the dark money super PACs backing him have been flooding
Alaska’s airwaves with lies to try and stop our momentum. And this shows
that their attacks are working...

This team has been key to our response. With your help, we’ve launched new
TV and digital ads and traveled hundreds of miles by plane, boat,
snowmachine, and more to rally our support across Alaska.

But we can’t stop here. These new numbers show that we have to push even
harder to overcome rampant outside spending in this race. Alaska is
shaping up to be the most competitive and expensive race on the map.

To fight back, we need to hit each and every one of our fundraising goals.
We’re coming up fast on our next FEC deadline with our biggest goal yet.
We’ll have to publicly report our fundraising for everyone to see, so we
need to show that we have what it takes to win.

That’s why we need a huge number of donations in response to this poll.
I’m counting on those of you who understand the importance of this race to
make a donation today before it’s too late. So I’m personally asking:

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260623-split.U7dtFf&refcode=em20260623-61570&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61570%2E1407376%2EDH-wuj ]Will you split a donation between Demand Justice PAC and my campaign
for U.S. Senate in Alaska? No matter how much you can afford to chip in
today, it all adds up when lots of us are chipping in.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260623-split.U7dtFf&amount=5&refcode=em20260623-61570&t=1022&akid=61570%2E1407376%2EDH-wuj ]Donate $5 ››

As long as we all work together, we will take back Alaska’s U.S. Senate
seat.

The strength of this campaign has always come from regular people stepping
up when it counted. And it means a lot to me that so many of you have
faith in our ability to win. Together, we’re building a movement.

Thanks for being a part of it.

- Mary

Team,
When you're running against an incumbent who has all the lobbyist checks in the world, along with his own millions to fall back on, there's no margin for error.
That's why we started early. For months, we've been getting our campaign out there, laying the groundwork, and building momentum one voter at a time.
**We 've been making big plans for this campaign and setting big goals to make them happen.**
_And we 've been crushing it._ We've blown past every benchmark so far and we beat Dan Meuser in individual contributions two quarters in a row. Now it's time to do it again.
**We 're one week away from our end-of-quarter FEC deadline.**
Our budgets are built around these deadlines. From the scale of our field program, to the number of yard signs we can buy, to our ability to push back when Dan Meuser starts spending his billionaire money against us - **everything depends on hitting this goal.**
There's no room to fall behind. So I need your help.

Peter - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington.

**I grew up in the back of a bar.**
Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill.

[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=575ddd55c19e478189e8f1121aed73a2&_e=SIh8mtQofEDLpwxrFLDAIA2VSLuaIne8nq1H2zicsMYL2onZFg6gJwI7cwW2AkoENgXkpdrh-H2U38qVx1EZLYM6VAI2cPXLNshG94kXWdBBWS4GJQLnmlG9SVd1aWFXtuqk2_KqV-pCbSSmdisOC9tuSBmCRAnSouJ8HObmNqj3iefXPv6Ia3Qy4zXUqDEdgSLTTGiwZLJJ7-gN7wBxgRFSPvYqbJscU9V0xTfzeYifDNOBT6dPoHuoPz0SM6RuEgjm6RRV9Bp33S7xhG8NjU_t6LvAiB8WxhFZu6pHbcGBEoFigOcJd0WM2OJVo_t4xWeJ9eR5ERVU3x85rbwkIDst91_CNIsLJwOYHVpTv7oG7ji-q60WaKEHq5ZSRBo4i5C1SAY5hfH8qFglmToOG5xuuVHoTN3hFfsp0rWsvhdgmu9ZjHVfWI_51QLyu63orPl1F5UsFH1vhuhr09MxdCNEzswrt8k6QzAZl7cdPTd9Qzj6evoc1_OpEJb-8-ykGH8dG2T4HTtBighQxSxzZZposIt9E09mfQmbNqXtuBRxRgNAPt73Z5kF0LWqqIbiudrOQEtmOpwsgyGSst7wHFns99iG7Kyi-NNLVpnZM6v9zPBylpNVO8t2IDmTDNOfnsAKZRRZhesrWZ1J8HmUPsOKTscrUMVrD0a30MMduzNl4EYfzW6SIizUD6HJptC6hJUyGyYBwZjW27l4I3QLNQ5yhN8tK_10TWMwMgw_S-WaUR2vKM_DeP_Cxf3EnjCNVzZwtgpw_AgHIcxJyokKe97ojtFL7_Ts7vgRxgoeoeGoPb2g-zqOov2avbKcOoRE)
Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did.

I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13.

I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb.

_**That's the South Carolina way. That's the American way.**_

After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves.

That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake.

The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today.

And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it.

clean_body: I fight so hard because I know what's at stake. | Peter - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington. I grew up in the back of a bar. Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did. I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13. I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb. That's the South Carolina way. That's the American way. After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves. That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake. The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today. And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it. I won't stand for it. Not for a second. We are in a fight for the future of this country, and it is not a time to sit on the sidelines. I didn't come from money. I came from a bar in South Carolina, a mother who worked hard, and a faith that hard work still means something in America. It still does. Thank you for standing with me. God bless you, and God bless South Carolina. I’ve spent my life fixing things that are broken.
On the factory floor.
In the Navy.
In the National Guard.
And right now, there’s nothing more broken than the United States Senate.
Washington isn’t working for people like us anymore. It’s working for billionaires, lobbyists, and corporations that write the rules for themselves — and leave the rest of us footing the bill.
I’m Dan Osborn, and I’m running for Senate to fix Washington. Please, chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can right now to help me → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
I’m not a career politician. I’m an industrial mechanic from Omaha, a former union leader who took on Kellogg’s to protect my coworkers’ wages and benefits, and a guy who knows what it means to work 80-hour weeks just to keep a middle-class life together.
And I’m running as an independent because I don’t owe either party a damn thing.
I owe you.
I’ll fight to cut taxes for working families, protect Social Security, stand up for family farms, and finally pass Right to Repair so corporations stop ripping people off just to fix what they own.
But I can’t do this alone. The same billionaires who broke Washington are going to spend whatever it takes to keep it that way.
So I’m asking: Will you chip in $10, $25, or anything you can right now to help us build a campaign that answers to working people — not the powerful? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
Let's fix this.

I’m proud to fight for Black maternal health alongside Cori and Eboni, who’ve championed this issue for many years. They understand how urgently we must dismantle racism in healthcare and ensure health equity for people of all backgrounds.
The three of us also know that, like ICE, our racist criminal legal system often brutally separates families.
We’re pushing for a government that invests in our communities’ needs — such as housing, healthcare, childcare, and education—rather than spending more of our tax dollars on state violence or for-profit corporations.
Together we’re working to save lives and secure dignity and safety for all people.
