clean_body: I’m proud to endorse Cori and Eboni for Congress and State Senate, where they’ll be champions for the people. | | | Friend, I’m proud to endorse two Black women running for office who recognize that our communities need transformative changes: Cori Bush and Eboni Taylor. Last week in St. Louis, I campaigned with Cori Bush, who’s running for Congress after AIPAC spent $9 million to defeat her: While serving in Congress, Cori Bush led the push for our shared humanity with bold legislation to guarantee housing and utilities as human rights, enact reparations and reproductive justice, demand a permanent and real ceasefire in Gaza, and transform our country’s approach to public safety to center care rather than criminalization. And whenEboni Taylor served as the Michigan Executive Director of Mothering Justice, she and I worked together to co-create the Congressional Mamas’ Caucus , which fights for mothers of color and working families. Now she works with Higher Heights for America to help elect Black women across the country, and she’s running for Michigan’s State Senate in a highly contested race where every dollar will count. Here’s a photo of me with Eboni Taylor and some of her family: Eboni, Cori, and I are fighting for Medicare for All, universal childcare and early education, and environmental justice—and against AI data centers, genocide, mass incarceration, and immigration detention. ** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, split evenly between Cori Bush, Eboni Taylor, and Rashida Tlaib. | | | | | | | | | | I’m proud to fight for Black maternal health alongside Cori and Eboni, who’ve championed this issue for many years. They understand how urgently we must dismantle racism in healthcare and ensure health equity for people of all backgrounds. The three of us also know that, like ICE, our racist criminal legal system often brutally separates families. We’re pushing for a government that invests in our communities’ needs — such as housing, healthcare, childcare, and education—rather than spending more of our tax dollars on state violence or for-profit corporations. Together we’re working to save lives and secure dignity and safety for all people. None of us take any money from corporate PACs, so we rely on grassroots support to run our election campaigns. With mail-in ballots getting to voters in Michigan and Missouri this week, right now is a crucial time for us to connect with our communities and let them know about our August 4th primary elections. Thank you for supporting candidates who are deeply committed to being public servants and rooted in their communities! It’s an honor to serve you in Congress and to know you’re by my side, fighting for a better world. With you in the fight, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib**** Date: Mon, Jun 22, 2026 Subject: Mail-in ballots are coming this week in Michigan and Missouri To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, I was just in St. Louis to campaign with Cori Bush and our former colleague Jamaal Bowman. AIPAC spent $26 million to defeat them, but Cori refused to back down: She’s running for Congress again. I’m also proud to endorse Eboni Taylor , a lifelong Detroiter like me who’s running for Michigan’s State Senate. When she served as the Michigan Executive Director of Mothering Justice, we worked together to co-create the Congressional Mamas’ Caucus, which fights for mothers of color and working families. Here’s a photo of Eboni and me with her family: Both Cori and Eboni are pushing back against AI data centers and our country’s punitive systems of mass incarceration and detention. They’re both speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and demanding universal healthcare and childcare here at home. We need these women in public office to keep building power against fascism and for the transformative changes our communities deserve. This week, voters in both Michigan and Missouri will receive mail-in ballots. Since none of us take money from corporate PACs, the three of us need grassroots support to connect with voters between now and our August 4th primary elections. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, split evenly between Cori Bush, Eboni Taylor, and Rashida Tlaib. | | | | | | | | | As the Vice President of Programs at Higher Heights for America, Eboni helps get Black women elected across the country. And as a leader at Mothering Justice, she helped mothers of color across our state survive and thrive, including securing paid sick time. If elected, Eboni will be the only mother from our area in the State Senate, where she’ll continue her work fighting for Black maternal health and reproductive rights. This is especially necessary here in Detroit, where pregnant Black women are 4.5 times more likely to die than white women — even higher than the shameful national average. Cori has written and spoken about how she nearly lost both of her children at childbirth due to anti-Black racism. As she explains: "Every day, Black women are subjected to harsh and racist treatment during pregnancy and childbirth. Every day, Black women die because the system denies our humanity." We must act now to save lives. Nearly 90 percent of pregnancy-related deaths are preventable, and I’ll keep fighting alongside Cori and Eboni for Black mothers and children, health equity, and an end to systemic racism. You’ve probably heard about the beautiful little boy Kohen Wiley, a 1-year-old who was killed by a white police officer last week. Outrageously, the officer shot into a car he mistakenly thought had stolen diapers. We will keep saying Kohen’s name and demanding justice for him and for all Black people killed by the police. We affirm that Black lives matter and are not disposable, and recommit to holding police accountable! After police killed Michael Brown, street medic Cori Bush joined the Ferguson Uprising, where she experienced police brutality herself. This lived experience spurred her national leadership for a public safety system rooted in care rather than punishment. Cori, Eboni, and I will not back down in the fight for true public safety and for our constitutional rights, including the right to protest and due process. We are pushing for a government that invests in our communities’ needs — such as housing, healthcare, and education — rather than continually spending more of our tax dollars on state violence. Thank you for helping to get these Black moms and powerful advocates into office. They’re deeply rooted in their communities, and their lived experiences shape their empathy for people of all backgrounds. We need them in the halls of power as we build a truly multi-racial democracy that serves all Americans, including the working class — rather than catering to corporate elites. In solidarity, Rashida * Rashida Tlaib for Congress PO Box 32777 Detroit, MI 48232 | Paid for by Rashida Tlaib for Congress | | Sent via . Hey folks,
A few days ago, New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani gave a speech celebrating the Knicks' championship run that immediately blew up online. People loved it. MAGA media hated it. And after sitting with it for a few days, I think the reaction tells us something much bigger than just sports.
This wasn't really about basketball. It was about storytelling, identity, and why some political leaders connect with people in ways others simply can't. If you missed this one the first time around, it's worth going back to. The conversation is just as relevant now as it was when it happened.
**Here 's the breakdown:**
* [**00:01:08**] Mamdani breaks down the Knicks' impossible comeback and turns a 0.4% chance into a rallying cry for New Yorkers everywhere.
* [**00:03:50**] The speech shifts from sports to something deeper--what it means to fight through impossible odds and keep showing up anyway.
* [**00:05:10**] I explain why this speech is actually a masterclass in political storytelling and movement-building.
* [**00:06:45**] I get into why Trump and the MAGA ecosystem seem obsessed with moments like this--and why cultural relevance matters more than they want to admit.
* [**00:11:20**] The conversation ends with a bigger question: why are some leaders focused on helping people while others are focused on staying in the spotlight?

This episode is really about authenticity. We break down what made Mamdani's speech resonate so deeply, why it triggered such a strong response from conservative media, and what it reveals about leadership, culture, and political communication in 2025. The headlines may have moved on, but the lessons here haven't. After Lead Maine submitted two rule-making petitions to DHHS, Nick Murray, Policy & Communications Director, said the goal is to restore accountability to MaineCare providers receiving taxpayer money. The proposals would require actual on-site inspections and suspend payments to providers suspected of improper billing before more money goes out the door. Meanwhile, after Jon Fetherston and Graham Pollard stop in Sullivan, several fishermen said Graham Platner's "oysterman" image does not match the reality of Maine's working waterfront. Their comments raised questions about Platner's campaign biography, his family safety net, his lack of advocacy for fishermen and whether real working-class Mainers feel represented by his anti-billionaire message.

Friends, tomorrow is a big day for my friend and colleague, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver. She’s heading back to court to take on Donald Trump's vindictive attacks against her for doing her job and speaking out against the treatment of detainees at Delaney Hall detention center.
Donald Trump wants to make us feel alone and isolated, and to make an example out of LaMonica to send a message about what happens when we speak out against him. But she is not alone — she has a community of supporters who are committed to fighting back against this cruel and corrupt administration. And right now, she needs our help.
LaMonica has had to raise her own legal defense — which has already exceeded a million dollars in fees — dollar by dollar, while still showing up every single day to work on behalf of the people of NJ-10. Will you split a donation between LaMonica’s campaign and mine before she heads into court? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em-mciver]
CHIP IN [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em-mciver]
In case you need a quick reminder of what’s at stake: LaMonica McIver is a wife, a mom (with another little one on the way!), and a freshman Congresswoman representing New Jersey’s 10th District. Last year, she joined her New Jersey colleagues in conducting a routine congressional oversight visit of Delaney Hall, an ICE detention facility in her district, after reports of detainees being unable to reach their lawyers.
Their delegation was met with resistance and aggression from ICE agents, and afterwards, the Trump administration charged LaMonica with completely baseless criminal charges. If convicted, she faces up to 17 years in prison.
Trump’s attacks against a sitting Congresswoman who refused to look away are unprecedented and dangerous. We must fight back for LaMonica and for the future of our democracy.
Will you show your support by making a contribution to our campaigns before her court hearing? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em-mciver]

body:
Seattle home prices are down, but rent is still squeezing working families dry.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260623-6386-footer&t=1&akid=6386%2E420207%2ETML_O5)
Peter,
Seattle home prices just hit the largest drop in the country, and now housing inventory is on the rise.
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260623.V0RjaA&refcode=em20260623-6386&t=2&akid=6386%2E420207%2ETML_O5)
Corporate landlords and Wall Street investors have spent years buying up single family homes and rental units across the country, turning entire neighborhoods into their own personal cash flows and locking working families out of home ownership.
While working families fall further and further behind, Trump and his billionaire buddies keep getting richer off of tax breaks built for the wealthy and watch their investment portfolios grow. **That is the tale of two housing markets in this country. One for the ultra rich — and one for everyone else.**
We have to be clear about what this new trend means and what it doesn’t.
Seattle is still one of the most expensive housing markets in the entire country. And while home prices are cooling down, rent is still sky high.
**Renters across our region and this country are still handing over more than they can afford, every single month, just to keep a roof over their heads. Housing should never be anything less than a human right, but it’s still being treated like a commodity.**
I refuse to lose sight of that.
That drop in home prices does nothing for the millions of renters who are barely getting by or the hundreds of thousands of people sleeping without shelter tonight. In the richest country in the world, that’s not a housing market problem. _It’s a deep and glaring moral failure._
**That’s exactly why I introduced the Housing is a Human Right Act in Congress.**
It would pour over $300 billion into housing infrastructure and homelessness services — because no one should have to “earn” a roof over their head and a safe place to sleep at night. It’s a basic human dignity that belongs to every single person in this country. Full stop.
We have more work to do — a lot more. But I’m not backing down from this fight, and I need you in it with me.
[**If you’re able, will you pitch in $3, or whatever is meaningful to you today, to help me keep fighting in Congress to make housing a human right for every person in this country?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260623.V0RjaA&refcode=em20260623-6386&amount=3&t=3&akid=6386%2E420207%2ETML_O5)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260623.V0RjaA&amount=3&refcode=em20260623-6386&t=22&akid=6386%2E420207%2ETML_O5)**
Thank you,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260623-6386-footer&t=23&refcode2=6386_420207_TML_O5&akid=6386%2E420207%2ETML_O5)**

ormation and upcoming events.

MOMENTUM WHEN IT MATTERS

Hi friends,

Campaigns are picking up speed this time of year, and we're on the move. We=
can't be everywhere, but we are certainly trying! Volunteers have already =
begun representing Team Barlow at parades, door-knocking, and community eve=
nts around Wyoming, and Kelly and I will join in as many places as we can.

Last week, I joined fellow candidates in Dubois for the Wyoming Republican =
Party gubernatorial debate. With early voting just a month away, people are=
paying closer attention to the choices ahead.

Ahead of the debate, our campaign released a Wyoming Republican Platform Sc=
orecard. You can find it [HERE](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/689e=
bd35962a1e6a80b1fecb/t/6a349ce686283c148d804861/1781832934911/GOP+Barlow+Pl=
atform_FINAL.docx.pdf).

We released the scorecard for a simple reason: records matter.

Campaigns are full of promises about what candidates will do. The scorecard=
focuses on what I've already done. It highlights recent legislation tied t=
o all 23 planks of the GOP platform. I covered bills I sponsored or co-spon=
sored, which advanced conservative priorities, including life, the Second A=
mendment, private property rights, religious freedom, election integrity, t=
ax relief, support for veterans, natural resources, education, and economic=
freedom.

Taking the oath of office and serving in the Legislature taught me that vot=
ing is only part of the job. The real work happens long before a bill reach=
es the floor. It requires listening, learning, building consensus when poss=
ible, and standing firm when necessary, especially when a bill has a mislea=
ding title, is unconstitutional, or is drafted by non-Wyoming interests. I'=
ll bring this approach to the governor's office.

REGISTER TO VOTE

If you haven't registered to vote, now is the time. Early voting begins Jul=
y 21, and the Republican Primary Election is August 18. I encourage everyon=
e to make a plan to vote and take part in shaping Wyoming's future. If you'=
re already registered, ask your family members, neighbors, and the young pe=
ople in your circle to register as well.

Thank you for your support, your prayers, and the many conversations we've =
shared across this great state.

-Eric

=E2=80=8B

In Case You Missed it...

Barlow Releases GOP Platform Scorecard=E2=80=8B

June 18, 2026 - Ahead of tonight=E2=80=99s Republican gubernatorial debate,=
Republican candidate Sen. Eric Barlow released a Wyoming Republican Platfo=
rm Scorecard showing a record of advancing conservative legislation on 100%=
of the planks during his tenure in the Wyoming Legislature.

The scorecard reviews all 23 planks of the Wyoming Republican Party platfor=
m and highlights accomplishments from Barlow=E2=80=99s legislative record. =
It shows that Barlow has not just voted for but also sponsored or co-sponso=
red legislation tied to 21 planks of the GOP platform, leading the way on c=
onservative issues.

=E2=80=9CVoting is important, but it=E2=80=99s only one part of legislating=
,=E2=80=9D Barlow said. =E2=80=9CThe work starts long before a bill ever re=
aches the floor. Serving people is about more than saying what you believe.=
It is about listening, learning, and doing the work =E2=80=94 and I=E2=80=
=99ve done that in a respectful and effective manner.=E2=80=9D

The scorecard includes legislation related to life, the Second Amendment, p=
rivate property rights, religious freedom, medical freedom, economic freedo=
m, federalism, military and veterans issues, tax relief, education, natural=
resources, right to work, free speech, and election integrity.

Barlow said the scorecard reflects the way he has served: with conservative=
principles, respect for the Constitution, conviction in faith, and a respo=
nsibility to his community and the people of Wyoming.

Barlow said that same approach applies to the budget, where many of the big=
gest policy decisions are made.

=E2=80=9CBudget votes are policy votes,=E2=80=9D Barlow said. =E2=80=9CWhat=
we fund, what we cut, and what we push back onto local communities all hav=
e real consequences. I have worked through those decisions, and done my bes=
t to understand what they mean for Wyoming families and communities.=E2=80=
=9D

Barlow recently signed the Peacemaker pledge, which reflects his belief tha=
t leaders can stand firm in their principles without treating people like e=
nemies.

=E2=80=9CWyoming is not helped by more anger or division,=E2=80=9D Barlow s=
aid. =E2=80=9CWe need to lower the temperature, tell the whole truth, and d=
o the work. That is how I have done my job as a Representative, Speaker of =
the House, and Senator, and that is how I will lead as governor.=E2=80=9D

The full scorecard is available [HERE](https://static1.squarespace.com/stat=
ic/689ebd35962a1e6a80b1fecb/t/6a349ce686283c148d804861/1781832934911/GOP+Ba=
rlow+Platform_FINAL.docx.pdf).

CASPER
Kelly and I enjoyed the evening at the College National Finals Short Go

It is an exciting opportunity to see firsthand the dedication, work ethic, =
and talent of Wyoming=E2=80=99s student athletes.

DUBOIS
I was in Dubois last week for the GOP gubernatorial candidate debate. You c=
an watch it online here at=C2=A0[County10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=
=3Dy805InM6ArI).

We talked through a variety of topics, including education, land rights, an=
d property tax balance, as well as growing a business-friendly economy in W=
yoming, which will keep our youth here for the future.

Debates matter, but experience counts. I have spent my time in the legislat=
ure proving my value with results, not just talk. 66 bills, all started thr=
ough constituent conversations, because that is what service looks like.

CHEYENNE

I joined the Wyoming Trial Lawyers legislative panel alongside Senator Barr=
y Crago and Senate Majority Floor Leader Tara Nethercott.

There was good discussion on the issues facing Wyoming's legal system and t=
he people it serves. Always good to share the table with colleagues who car=
e about getting it right for Wyoming

WHEATLAND

I toured the Basin Power Project in Wheatland.

Wyoming's energy future depends on responsible development and keeping deci=
sions close to home. It was good to see that work up close and talk with th=
e people making it happen

CHEYENNE

I attended the Wyoming Trial Lawyers Association convention reception in Ch=
eyenne.

Good conversations with attorneys from across the state who care about Wyom=
ing's legal system and the people it serves. Always good to hear from diffe=
rent corners of Wyoming on the issues that matter most

WHEATLAND

I had a meet and greet in Wheatland and joined the seniors for lunch at the=
senior center.

Always good to sit down with folks who have spent a lifetime building and s=
erving Wyoming communities. The conversations at those tables are always ho=
nest and always worthwhile.

UPTON

I visited a rare earth plant with Rare Element Resources and toured their m=
ine and plant at Warren Peak.

Wyoming sits on some of the most valuable mineral resources in the country,=
and I have consistently supported legislation protecting and enhancing Wyo=
ming=E2=80=99s mineral development.

The opportunity here is real.

CHEYENNE

Great evening at the Laramie County Republican Party Cookout with the Candi=
dates at Lions Park in Cheyenne.We appreciate our volunteers showing up for=
Team Barlow.

Good food, good people, and good conversations with folks who showed up to =
get informed and get involved. That is what this process is supposed to loo=
k like.

Thank you to the LCGOP for putting it together and to everyone who came out=
.

CROOK COUNTY
Kelly and I had a full day across Crook and Weston counties.

We started with a meet and greet in Pine Haven, then headed to Moorcroft fo=
r an ice cream meet and greet that afternoon. We wrapped up the evening wit=
h another meet and greet in Upton.

Three communities, a lot of good conversations and great people at every st=
op. Thank you to everyone who came out to visit with us.

DAYTON

We had a beautiful evening in Dayton recently. Many thanks to all who showe=
d up to ask questions about education, healthcare, industry and more.

A granddaughter of an attendee popped up with a question of her own, asking=
, =E2=80=9CWhy are you running for Governor?=E2=80=9D There=E2=80=99s only =
one answer: for her future!

Thank you to the Dayton community, our hosts, Cody and Sarah Jo Sinclair, a=
nd those who joined from the surrounding communities

IT'S PARADE SEASON!!

Burns Day

The annual Burns Day parade and activities is always a great Wyoming Day! C=
andy and frisbees made for a lot of fun for campaign volunteers and support=
ers! Thanks for having us!

Greybull Days of =E2=80=9849!

Parade days are here, and the Barlow campaign was READY with candy and fris=
bees!

Thanks to Jamie Flitner and our Big Horn County volunteers, the Days of '49=
were a great success. What a good-looking parade set up!

Happy Pride Month!
As we step into this vibrant and vital time of year, we celebrate all of the LGBTQIA+ members of our St. Louis community and across the country who enrich our lives every single day.
But, Peter—Pride Month is not just a celebration; it is a commemoration of a struggle. This is the result of organizing, uprising, and activism rooted in the Stonewall Riots. We must never forget that Pride started as a protest against police violence and LGBTQIA+ discrimination. And fifty-seven years later, we are still fighting the GOP’s extremist efforts to restrict the rights of our LGBTQIA+ community.
I, for one, have made it my mission to fight every day to reject the GOP's attacks against the LGBTQIA+ community and push for a more just, inclusive, and equitable society.
In Missouri and across the country, we are witnessing a terrifying rise in anti-trans legislation and hate crimes. But our movement is a movement of love that protects all of humanity, and together, we are advocating for policies that proudly declare that Trans Lives Matter and Black Trans Lives Matter. I will keep emphasizing the need to protect and uplift these communities, because every person has the right to live their life as their true, authentic selves.
Our collective fight for justice and freedom is why I support H.R. 15, the Equality Act , which seeks to provide consistent and explicit anti-discrimination protections for LGBTQIA+ people across key areas of life. When I was in office, I led the push to finally certify and publish the ERA (Equal Rights Amendment) , striving for constitutional recognition of gender equality—and I will continue to do so when I’m back in office.
Can I count on you to donate to my campaign today, so I can continue to lead the charge for equality and advocate for our LGBTQIA+ communities in Congress? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q2?refcode=x_260623_pride_act]

Hi Peter,
I’m reaching out personally today to ask for your help — but before I do,
let me explain a few things.

This email isn’t being sent to our full list of supporters. I’m messaging
a few select folks, including you,
Peter, who haven’t yet
contributed to our campaign.

I understand if there hasn’t been a good time to give up to this point.
Maybe you wanted to see some polling before pitching in, or wanted to wait
until Election Day was closer. Both valid reasons to wait.

But now, we need you. AIPAC has already spent $21 million on ads to stop
us, and that amount is expected to balloon up to $30 million by the time
this race is over.

That’s why I urgently need your help,
Peter. We’re leading in both
the primary and general polls, and absentee ballots start mailing out this
Thursday — it’s all gas and no brakes from here on.

This is the most pivotal moment of our campaign, and if there were ever a
time to make your first donation, it's now.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260623-2-ak._NMU5_&amount=10&refcode=em20260623-2425&t=1004&akid=2428%2E251025%2EhtEvPz ]So please, can you make your first donation of $25, $10, or even just
$1 today?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260623-2-ak._NMU5_&amount=10&refcode=em20260623-2425&t=1023&akid=2428%2E251025%2EhtEvPz ]Donate $10 ››

The only way we’ll win this race and overcome the massive amounts of
spending against us is if we band together.

Thank you so much,

Abdul

P.S. If you've donated very recently or with a different email address,
please know that we received your contribution and are so grateful for the
support. 🙏

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Wall Street Is Sitting on a $3 Trillion Problem It Hopes You Never Notice The people who study 2008 for a living are using that word again. There's a corner of the financial world most Americans have never heard of. It's called private credit. Lending done in the shadows, away from public markets and the rules that govern banks. It grew into a $3 trillion market while almost nobody was watching. Now the cracks are showing. In April 2026, Fitch reportedly confirmed defaults inside private credit hit a record 6 percent. UBS has projected they may climb toward 9 to 10 percent before the year is out. New issuance reportedly fell from about $74 billion to $44 billion in a single quarter. Here's the part that should make you sit up. Some of the biggest names on Wall Street, Blackstone, Apollo, Ares, and KKR, have reportedly seen redemption requests blow past their own 5 percent caps. When that happens, the gate comes down. Investors who want their money are told to wait. BlueOwl reportedly froze redemptions outright. CNN has run the phrase "echoes of 2008." A London Business School professor went on CNBC and drew a direct line to 2007. The Economist warned of the pain still to come. Analysts at LSEG have openly asked whether private credit is simply subprime wearing a new suit. If that comparison sounds familiar, it should. The last time Wall Street sold risk it didn't fully understand as safe, the people who paid the price were ordinary savers. And roughly $807 billion of this private credit money is reportedly tied to life insurance balance sheets. The same kind of products quietly backing retirement income for millions. Now contrast that with an asset that can't be gated, can't be frozen, and can't be printed into existence by anyone. Physical gold. You don't have to take our word for it. According to State Street, central banks bought roughly 244 tonnes of gold in the first quarter of 2026 alone. They aren't chasing a fad. body:
The DOJ just indicted child smugglers hiding in plain sight as "sponsors." Here's what you need to know and what you can do right now.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e13901341/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvdjZLdXZ4R2I3eg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA2MjM/LbmNseWdCU1JXOA/qP2hpZHM9bmMwWnJTMzUxSUJYNnhscw/gajsHoQ/semc8bc3347)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, **300,000 children are missing.** Not lost. **Taken**. Trafficked by criminals who called themselves "sponsors." **Predators in disguise.** Last week, the DOJ pulled back the curtain on how it happened. Their announcement should stop every parent, every grandparent, and every person of faith in their tracks. And the number that haunts me most: **15,500** That is how many so-called **"super sponsor"** cases the DOJ has now uncovered. These are individuals who fraudulently sponsor multiple unaccompanied migrant children, and are linked to the trafficking of hundreds of thousands of children. **Illegal criminals who took custody of multiple unrelated migrant children using stolen identities, fake documents, and outright lies.** _And nearly 300,000 of those children are still unaccounted for._
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
My name is _Eduardo Verástegui._ I produced the film _Sound of Freedom_ because I believe the world needed to see this evil for what it is. The film woke millions of people up. But what the DOJ just revealed tells us the fight is far from over.
---
[ Stand for God's Children Now ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Friend, these were not nameless statistics crossing a distant border. **They were children. Created by God, loved by God.** And last week, we learned exactly how they were taken. A family network including a woman and her brother ran a smuggling network out of Ohio. They are accused of deceiving the Office of Refugee Resettlement with forged documents to secure custody of minors . Attorney General Todd Blanche said it plainly: these children were _"abused, assaulted, and certainly exploited."_ But this is not an isolated case. **This is a system**. **A criminal network that preys on the most vulnerable children in the world and hides behind paperwork to do it.** That is the reality Sound of Freedom has been fighting to expose since before the cameras ever rolled. **And today, you have the chance to fight this network of abuse.**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
The **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to send one distinct message: **God's children are not for sale.** Your support helps fund the search for these missing children. When you stand with us today, you are not just donating. You are sending a message to traffickers, politicians, and every child still waiting to be found. There are people in this world who will not look away. **[Friend, will you make your first gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever God places on your heart today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ Stand for God's Children Now ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Every dollar you give helps:
---
* Search for children who are still missing
* Rescue victims trapped in trafficking networks
* Restore the lives of survivors through aftercare and support
* Fund awareness efforts that expose traffickers before they can strike again.

---
The DOJ has reminded us that the threat is real. **Now it is up to people like you to make sure the fight continues.**
---
Scripture says: _"Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute."_ (Proverbs 31:8) Join me and speak up today. With gratitude and prayer,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation
---
_P.S. The DOJ's announcement confirmed what I have believed for years: this evil is real, it is organized, and it is hiding in plain sight. That is why I made a promise to God to help stop the sale of God's children. Your support today helps ensure these children are seen, protected, and never forgotten._
---
[ Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074
---

Hi there, it’s
Jocelyn Benson.

As a marathoner hoping to be Michigan’s next governor, I spend a lot of
time running, both in the political and literal sense.

Throughout our campaign I’ve had the chance to run with voters in run
clubs all across Michigan. I have the chance to get my athletic time in,
and more importantly, hear directly from Michiganders at the same time. As
we run, we talk about the challenges folks are facing, and their hopes for
the future.

Each mile and every conversation proves this campaign is a lot like
running a marathon.

It’s not about how fast you can sprint, but about showing up, staying
steady, and refusing to give up. It takes discipline, resilience, and
willingness to keep going even when things get tough.

I’ve run more than 40 marathons in my life, and this is the most important
race I’ve run yet, because I’m running to make Michigan the best place to
be a kid, raise a kid, and call home for all Michiganders.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/6944?t=1002&akid=1693%2E181023%2EAn0sLT ]But, I can’t win this race alone. We’re building a campaign powered by
people, not special interests, that’s strong enough to take on the outside
money pouring into Michigan. Can I count on you to chip in $25 to help us
keep building the campaign we need to cross the finish line this November?

# **JPMorgan DEI executive fired after Knicks parade trash can theft goes viral**
Angie Baez, 40, an Executive Director at JPMorgan Chase overseeing community and industry engagement, **[was terminated Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/89e47da5-020c-4830-b12b-224a21e72a15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after video surfaced showing her dumping the contents of a limited-edition Knicks-themed trash can onto a Manhattan sidewalk during the NBA championship parade before walking off with the bin. Another clip showed her riding the subway with the stolen trash can.

* **JPMorgan confirmed her departure after reviewing the incident,** noting she had attended the parade in a personal capacity. clean_body: Congress failed to ask the right questions before Iraq. | | Friend, Almost 25 years ago, Congress voted to send me and more than 100,000 other Americans to war in Iraq. They did it based on faulty intelligence and a lot of lies. They did it because too many people in Washington failed to ask the questions they were supposed to ask. Senator Markey was one of them. Now, even with talk of a new Iran deal, we still do not have the answers the American people deserve. Trump brought us into another war in the Middle East without the authorization of Congress. And a new deal does not erase how we got here. We cannot let this become the norm again. Congress has to make sure no President can do this again and call it a victory after the fact. Massachusetts deserves a senator who understands that asking hard questions before a war starts is not optional. It is the job. = | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately. I can't thank you enough.
I am beyond grateful for your support. It is the fuel that keeps our campaign moving.
I wake up every morning driven by a single purpose: making a real difference in your life and protecting the values we hold dear in Maine.
When I made the decision to run, I knew the attacks would be relentless. I am confident in my decision because I know I am not standing alone.
You have my back, and I have yours.
Together, we are a firewall protecting our common sense decisions. Again, thank you for standing with me. I would not be where I am today without your support.
Sincerely,
Susan Collins

body:
__**FROM THE DESK OF MLB LEGEND MARK TEIXEIRA**__

People often say that hitting a baseball is among the hardest things to do in sports.

After nearly two decades in Major League Baseball facing the best pitchers on the planet, I can tell you it certainly isn't easy.

But the truth is, it pales in comparison to the real challenges and rewards of the American Dream: raising a family, building a business, supporting your neighbors, and helping preserve the greatest country the world has ever known.

Those experiences have shaped me far more than any home run, championship, or All-Star appearance ever could.

My name is Mark Teixeira. Many of you know me from my years in Major League Baseball, including my time with the Texas Rangers. But with the help of great American patriots like you, I'm hoping to join President Trump's MAGA majority in Congress.

I had the privilege of playing for what I believe is the greatest franchise in sports, and every time I stepped onto the field, I understood I was representing something bigger than myself.

Today, I'm seeking the opportunity to represent something even greater: the United States of America.

I was fortunate to play for legendary managers who demanded excellence, expected accountability, and never lost sight of winning. President Trump brings that same mentality to leadership: setting high standards, challenging the status quo, and focusing on results.

Just as the Yankees set the standard for excellence in baseball, America has long set the standard for freedom, opportunity, and self-government. Both are built on proud traditions, high expectations, and the belief that every generation has a responsibility to leave things better than they found them.

That's why I'm running.

If you're ready to help bring common-sense conservative leadership and a commitment to service to Congress, I hope you'll stand with me today by making a contribution to our campaign.

Thank you, and God bless America.

Sincerely,

Mark Teixeira

subject: I should have done more call time
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260623-2952)
Peter,
We’ve got a big goal. I want to be totally upfront - it’s our largest goal yet, and it's critical.
[**We need to raise $100,000 before midnight on June 30th, and we need your help.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/14471?t=1&akid=2952%2E105371%2EuXw1qa)
[**If you’re able to give now, please help us reach this goal.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/14471?t=2&akid=2952%2E105371%2EuXw1qa)
Why this goal, and why now? At midnight on June 30th, the books will close on the whole first half of this year. It will be the first (and largest) publicly-reported fundraising deadline in 2026. It will be the moment where we decide whether we can purchase more literature, send out digital ads, and fund our office space through August. It’ll be a moment where folks will take a look at our campaign (and the whole field) and make decisions on if we’re viable.
**_This week is going to be a big decision maker on whether or not we can win._**
[**__**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260622.CCiiT8&refcode=em20260623-2952&t=3&akid=2952%2E105371%2EuXw1qa)
Our campaign is one of service, and we’ve built amazing relationships by showing up in communities and doing the work that brings people together. If I’m being totally honest, I’ve taken call time off my calendar to put time with people on it.
I need your support to make up a big gap so we can compete with our opponent’s dark-money groups, and wealthy backers. [**I will always get more excited packing up period supplies than asking for dollars - but your contribution of $25, $40, or more if you’re able is essential if we want to get the word out across Wisconsin.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260622.CCiiT8&refcode=em20260623-2952&t=4&akid=2952%2E105371%2EuXw1qa)
We’re closing in on a moment that is going to define our campaign and we appreciate all of your support.
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260622.CCiiT8&amount=5&refcode=em20260623-2952&t=7&akid=2952%2E105371%2EuXw1qa)**
With gratitude,
\- Fran
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260623-2952&t=8&refcode2=2952_105371_uXw1qa&akid=2952%2E105371%2EuXw1qa)**
---
Email us: [info@francescahong.com](mailto:info@francescahong.com)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is one of the most powerful tools that grassroots campaigns like ours have to reach everyday people across Wisconsin and beyond, so thank you for reading to the end.
The more people who engage with our emails, the more likely we’ll go straight to your inbox. For a free and easy way to help our campaign, please [click this link to our website](https://francescahong.com/) after you finish reading our emails.
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.francescahong.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/)

Peter,

November is a Social Security Election.

Social Security is on track to run out of money by 2032, triggering automatic benefit cuts, so the future of this entire program will be in the hands of the Senators we elect this fall.
Democrats actually have plans to save Social Security for future generations, including scrapping the cap so the very wealthiest pay the same tax rate as everyone else.

Republicans have a different view. GOP mega-donor and the world’s first trillionaire, Elon Musk, called Social Security a “Ponzi scheme.” Trump’s Treasury Secretary has even suggested privatizing Social Security, and Speaker Johnson has already called for “adjustments” to Social Security – and we all know what that means: cuts.
In fact, unlike every President before him, Trump hasn’t even bothered to put forward a plan to keep Social Security solvent with his annual budget request to Congress – doing nothing before it’s too late means automatic benefit cuts.
**That’s where you come in.** With a Senate Democratic majority in the fall, we can take action to save Social Security and make sure it’s here for generations to come. NOW is the time to act. NOW is the time to make your voice heard.
[**If you’re with me in the fight to save Social Security, sign my petition before 11:59 p.m. tonight.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133879165/629390822/-348617454?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&code=jtk657-su-nd&sustainers=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNzUzNTU1Ni01NzZmLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kXuzVBgJI3hE996Q_fNGeqWENCYvh2-LzgNiys-KfLs=&emci=c1f5f3c4-516e-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=a7535556-576f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=13116610)

Hi, it’s Jon Ossoff. I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won. And this U.S. Senate race in Georgia will be the most competitive and most expensive in the nation. body:
This move strips nearly 2 million Tennesseans of the representation they deserve.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2301%2E791427%2E52fLNV)
Recently, I received official notice from Tennessee House Speaker Cameron Sexton that I had been **removed from all of my state House committee assignments — _alongside every other_ Tennessee House Democrat. **
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-pearson.3SBx88&refcode=em260623-2-30-90&t=2&akid=2301%2E791427%2E52fLNV)
This is one of the **_most troubling abuses of power_** in our state’s history.
[**This kind of retaliation only works if we let them intimidate us into silence. I won’t let it, but I’ll need your help to keep fighting.[**So if you’re able to, split $10 or more right now with our campaign and Ilhan Omar to keep our grassroots movement strong enough to defend ourselves and our communities from this authoritarian attack.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-pearson.3SBx88&refcode=em260623-2-30-90&t=4&akid=2301%2E791427%2E52fLNV) **[CONTRIBUTE $10 NOW](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/6171?c0=io-em-pearson.MvjHg-&refcode=em260623-2-30-90&t=5&akid=2301%2E791427%2E52fLNV)** If this sounds familiar, it should. Because this is what TN House Republicans do when they don’t like what you have to say. More than three years ago, they expelled me after I protested on the House floor against their inaction on gun violence. They thought they could make an example of me for _refusing_ to be quiet while our communities were hurting. _Now,_ they’re doing it all over again. In early May, they pushed through rigged, racist maps designed to _eliminate_ TN-09’s identity as a majority-Black, Democratic district. TN House Democrats stood together and made it clear that we would not stand for this injustice. So they retaliated. Committee assignments aren’t ceremonial positions. They’re how state lawmakers do the day-to-day work of representing our communities — from hearing bills, shaping policy, and fighting for the needs of the People who sent us there. But no matter what, they can’t strip away our voice, our courage, and our commitment to our People and neighborhoods. Civil rights icon and former Representative John Lewis taught us to make good trouble — necessary trouble. With your support, we’ll keep doing just that. name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: A big winter is coming.
body:
Plus: The DEA let 300,000 fentanyl pills walk into Albuquerque | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/9vloH0V_7QT?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
A big winter is locked in for New Mexico. So is a DEA scandal that should make every parent in this state furious.
[Mark walks through what a strong El Niño means for our snowpack, fire season, and ski mountains. ](https://us.list-manage.com/Oi611dnQJHJ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)Then we break down the Journal's front-page story on how the DEA let 300,000 deadly pills walk onto Albuquerque streets.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/hnXFQ262Oqf?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
❄️ **STRONG EL NIÑO IS LOCKED IN. NM COULD SEE 1997-98 LEVELS OF SNOW**
100% chance of El Niño through next spring. Mark pulled two analog years to compare. 1997-98 was the year Albuquerque doubled its monthly precip averages and the northern mountains were stacked. 2015-16 started strong, then February and March bottomed out and the snowpack vanished.
We tell you which year this winter is tracking toward, and why ski resorts in Wyoming, Idaho, and Utah are about to have a rough season.
---
| [Stream No Doubt About It Podcast Now](https://us.list-manage.com/ZNgOHX8ThuI?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🚨 **DEA LET 300,000 DEADLY PILLS WALK ONTO ALBUQUERQUE STREETS**
Front page of the Journal today. DEA agent David Howell filed a formal whistleblower complaint saying his own agency is letting fentanyl flow into Albuquerque on purpose.
The DEA's argument: you sometimes have to follow shipments to catch the bigger distributors. Howell's argument: they've tipped too far the other way. New Mexico's overdose deaths jumped 23% last year, the highest increase in the country.
The DEA issued two formal statements in 24 hours. We read both on air. Pay attention to what they don't deny.

🏛️ **TRUMP, VANCE, AND RUBIO ARE NOT SAYING THE SAME THING ON IRAN**
Trump told Iran's leadership "you won't even make it back to your effing country," then said the U.S. should take 20% of the oil that moves through the Strait of Hormuz.
JD Vance went on TV calling the return of IAEA inspectors a "major milestone." Marco Rubio? Different temperature entirely.
Mark thinks there's a real split inside the White House over how soft a deal to cut, and he names who lands where. Meanwhile, Iran's president just publicly said enrichment is non-negotiable.

🇺🇸 **TEAM ALGAE, A 250-FOOT GASH, AND THE 29% NUMBER**
Trump spent $14 million renovating the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. There's already a 250-foot gash in the new liner, and people are showing up with "Team Algae" signs. Jeanine Pirro says prosecutions are coming.
NBC's new pride-in-America poll: 90% of Republicans say they're proud of this country. Among Democrats? 29%.
---
| [Stream No Doubt About It Podcast Now](https://us.list-manage.com/L_Nn3jCcdYW?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🥲 **WISDOM TEETH DAY AT THE RONCHETTI HOUSE**
Both Ava and Ella got their wisdom teeth out the morning of the shoot. One came out laughing with the nurse, ready for a smoothie. The other one... let's just say Krysty could hear her from the lobby.

There's already a 250-foot gash in the new liner, and people are showing up with "Team Algae" signs. Jeanine Pirro says prosecutions are coming. Among Democrats? 29%. | | | 🥲 WISDOM TEETH DAY AT THE RONCHETTI HOUSE Both Ava and Ella got their wisdom teeth out the morning of the shoot.
